The Necessity of Organization for the Merchant Class

(On the activity and tasks of the Sosnowiec Small Traders' Association.)

The average merchant holds that a merchants' organization has only the task of handling the whole, "so to speak", legal side of the merchant. The association is the merchant's bookkeeper and lawyer (for this purpose there is indeed[?] active[?] at the Sosnowiec association a fairly large secretariat under the direction of the expert Mr. Kac, as well as 2 employed lawyers), but in our opinion the association also has many more important tasks to carry out, and it is about these that we wish to speak out here.

—

The former opinion in outside society about the uselessness of the merchant has changed radically. One realises[?] that on the direct path from producer to consumer the bureaucracy alone would swallow more than the present-day merchant's profit; in general the opinion about private initiative is changing. That is the reason for the frequent attacks on etatism [state control of the economy], which are aimed ever more often from the Sejm and from other public tribunes.

Former minister Mr. Klarner gave a major speech on the radio a few weeks ago, in which he stated, among other things, that the government and society have broken with their former opinion about the merchant class. The merchant, he said, is today regarded as a productive element, and as necessary as any other branch of the economy for the economic life of the country.

But if in outside society the former opinion about the unproductiveness of the merchant is being abandoned, among the Jewish merchant himself this opinion still persists.

One of the most important tasks of a merchants' organization is to raise the self-respect of the Jewish merchant in his own eyes, to change[?] his psychology, so that he should not feel in his calling like a fifth wheel on the economic wagon. And if the Jew will stress with self-pride the words "I am a merchant", then the attitude toward him will also have to be as toward one.

• • •

The Jewish merchant today finds himself between waves of old Jew-hatred and present-day competitive hatred, which has flooded[?] Polish society above all. The Jewish merchants of Zagłębie too already feel this heavily on their shoulders, especially in the suburbs, where the anti-Jewish campaign is already taking threatening forms, such as blockading Jewish shops, photographing customers, etc.

The Jewish merchants must therefore be united in large, strong organizations: the smaller and retail merchants in their association and the bigger ones in theirs, which should stand bravely and firmly on guard and not let their positions be undermined.

• • •

The trading system of the Jewish merchant, based on a small profit, is surely the strongest force that still sustains his existence, and also the strongest weapon against all anti-Jewish persecutions and boycotts. This price-cutting must, however, have a certain limit. Many times it is the result of a "neither for me nor for you" system [lit. "neither mine nor yours shall it be"], in which prices become simply absurd.

This matter too must be regulated by the merchants' organizations with the proper means.

• • •

Insofar as merchants' and small traders' associations already exist[?], their rational activity is hampered by the merchants and even by the members themselves, whose attitude to the whole matter is "leave me in peace".

For example: considering that the sword of the census law [the trade-qualification law] hangs over the head of the Jewish merchant, and that in the eventual examination knowledge of the commercial laws and of the Polish language will surely be required in the first place[?], the Small Traders' Association began to organise a cycle of lectures on economic-legal and tax topics. These lectures, given by first-class legal and oratorical talents, had to be cancelled, however, for lack of listeners. Likewise the Polish-language courses, organised at the time by the Small Traders' Association for its members and their families, were also discontinued for lack of pupils.

•

This attitude is for the most part the result of a critical attitude of our Jews toward every so-called "novelty". It seems to some ordinary Jews, and also to "more modern"[?] merchants, that just as their father and grandfather lived out their years without organizations, they too will manage without them...

— But at that time the merchant class — like professional life in general — was not yet hemmed in by such narrow legal frameworks as it is today. Moreover, the whole struggle against the Jew is today waged on economic ground, and [—][?] decrees small and large, which must be protested[?] in good time.

If all these indifferent people do not come to their senses and break[?] with their passivity and their [—] coldness toward their most vital interests, who knows whether it will not one day be too late...

As for how the internal work of the organizations should be set up — in the second article.

"Organizator" [pen name: "The Organizer"].
Create a Representation!

Remarks of a Sosnowiec communal worker.

From one of the Sosnowiec communal workers, who is especially popular on the economic front, we have received the following remarks on a topical subject. Ed.

Of every work, especially public work, a balance must be drawn at certain periods, in order to see whether the work is going right, and, if there are shortcomings, to remove them. That is why I come today to such a balance, although several weeks have already passed since New Year. But in my opinion, at the present time an accounting is necessary and possible, because we are not standing on the eve of any elections, there are therefore no ambitions, and on the Jewish street it is quiet, desperately quiet, and the need is even greater.

I recall: two years ago an acquaintance of mine took me into the premises of a Jewish society in Będzin, where I was present at a consultation about creating a Jewish representation in Zagłębie. I listened very seriously to the speeches of the initiators, then to a discussion which — merely when I recall it — still makes me blush with shame. I fled from the meeting with an unpleasant feeling, because for the first time I saw the mentality of the Jewish leaders of Zagłębie. I followed the matter itself and was content that the initiators were not me. Meanwhile, however, I left Sosnowiec and came back only two years later. I wanted to speak with the Jewish representation, and I learned that such a body... does not exist at all. I asked one of the initiators: why was the representation not created? The answer was given to me by a Jewish lawyer: he had called on the Jewish public to be cautious regarding the representation. But his voice was not heard on the Jewish street, because people like to play at opposition.

These days I visited several institutions. Once they flourished; today they cannot be recognised. I meet in the street an old economic activist, a man who carries on his shoulders 40 years of public work.

"You look very well," I say.

"Yes," he answers, "I feel well; I no longer work in the associations and societies, I no longer have 15 interventions and 10 meetings a day — I am resting."

"What does that mean?"

"Yes, to public work I could devote my time, strength and health, but not my honour. I work, I do what I can, I help where it is possible — thus I fulfil my duty; but I am not compelled to work together with squealers[?], shouters and those who delight in smearing someone."

I shook his hand and went off, thinking: does such a fate really await every Jewish communal worker!

But it is not so bad everywhere. I also visited the Jewish hospital, the "TOZ" [Jewish health society], the interest-free loan fund (Gemilut Chesed), and found that great things are being done there; that these institutions bring real, substantial help to the individual Jew as well as to the community.

And I also learned that at the head of these institutions stand people who devote themselves body and soul to the work, and whose tenacity breaks through all kinds of difficulties.

Bravo — I bow my head before them.

I turn to the Jewish intelligentsia in Sosnowiec: take up public work and place yourselves at the head of Jewish Zagłębie, organise a Jewish representation, and through work for the community you will earn the trust of the Jewish street, which calls on you and begs you to take up this work.

Dr. X.
Our Panorama

(The "kingdom" in the synagogue on Plac Sosnowiec. — Gentiles take delight as the "Żydy" [?, derogatory Polish for Jews] fight each other. — When someone is called up for shlishi, the answer is "nie pozwolen" [?, "I won't allow it"]. — Blows from the gabbaim. — Where are the sacred vessels?)
— "The Jewish state is on its way" — so the emissaries of Keren Hayesod announced to us this week, and we say that we are already a step further: the Jewish state already exists on Plac Sosnowiec, only our senses are so dulled that we do not feel it; for if we looked closely at what is happening before our eyes, we would see that we have a "kingdom" in all its details and particulars.
The worshippers in the synagogue on Plac Sosnowiec are known as quarrelsome elements. Already in the days when the "gubim" stood at the helm of the kehilla, bloody clashes often took place there. Things got worse when the kehilla passed into the hands of the appointees [the government-nominated board], whom the "people" refuse to recognize, wishing instead to found a separate "republic". Because of the aggravated situation the head of the kehilla has already come to the "front" several times and called on the "people" to make peace. But the call had the same effect as his "witty" articles "Na rzeczy" ["To the point"]..
— We want independent freedom! — answers the "people" — if we do not win it by peaceful means, we are ready for the greatest sacrifices.
And if you think these are empty phrases, you are badly mistaken. The Jewish element on Plac Sosnowiec does not let anyone blow into its porridge, and when the appointed gabbai took his stand on parashat Bo to distribute the aliyot, a signal was heard and the "people" went out to battle. The beginning took place indoors and the end — in the street; and why not, let the gentiles have a little pleasure, let them see how the "Żydy" [?] go at [?] each other..
It is only [?] a "lie" that the combatants did not also carry the Torah scroll out into the street, since the whole fight is, after all, over that little Torah..
According to the "latest" reports, a ceasefire has meanwhile been declared, and the "government" is being run by the cantor and the beadle.
— Well, should we be ashamed of "our kingdom"?
———
Not only of "our kingdom" should we be proud, but also of our communal activists, who possess a tremendous sense of smell and have the proper qualifications as "zhe-tshongovtses" [?, unclear nickname] for aliyot...
Once, when the spiritual state stood at the proper level, such "connoisseurs" were found in almost all houses of prayer and all minyanim, but gradually [?] their number is shrinking, and only in very large societies can one still find such a "maven".
Among the larger societies there undoubtedly belongs the "Linat ha-Holim" society in Sosnowiec, which runs an outpatient clinic and a minyan. The difference is only this: from the clinic the board has pleasure, and from the minyan — "troubles", because all the frictions around the society so far have arisen from the minyan, or more precisely, from the "constitution" of the minyan.
In accordance [printed "hefkem"] with the "constitution" it is the custom in this minyan that a person observing a yahrzeit that falls in the middle of the week receives an "ordinary" aliyah, i.e. shlishi or shishi; but if the yahrzeit falls on Sunday he receives maftir. This is already a tradition from days of old, from "the Creation" onward, and the congregation was content.
But times change. On Saturday, 1 February [1-ten luty], the situation changed, and little was lacking for the whole "constitution" on the distribution of aliyot to be changed. The cause was the gabbai, who honoured a board member, a "weekday yahrzeit-observer", with... shlishi.
— "Nie pozwolen" [?] — answered the yahrzeit-observer — the rules of the constitution are binding on the "people", but not on members of the government; I am not just anybody, after all"...
This "exposé" naturally aroused unrest in government circles. Is it proper to say "nie pozwolen" [?] while the Torah scroll lies on the table and the congregation waits for the blessing!.. It smacks of something [?]..., but the government circles succeeded in liquidating [the incident], and after a pause of 10 minutes the yahrzeit-observer agreed to shlishi, and all is firm and settled..
———
The gabbaim of the Będzin beit midrash face a difficult task: to establish where the sacred vessels of the beit midrash are.
When the present gabbaim took over power, they beheld a real [?] "wonder": the Holy Ark is always locked and the sacred vessels are gone.
Suspicion falls even on one of the former gabbaim, who, realizing [?] that his rule was falling, thought to himself: "My colleagues are idlers, but I know [—] [?]"... and wanted to hide the objects; nevertheless one cannot openly accuse a gabbai of the Będzin beit midrash of permitting himself to do such a thing...
As rumour has it, the gabbaim are to turn to the kehilla board with the request that the matter be handed over to the investigator of clandestine ritual slaughter. He will surely find out who took the sacred vessels...
Ben Amotz.
Zagłębie Jews Are Settling on the Land

[Palestine — immigration and settlement; Zagłębie emigrants.]
(From our Palestine correspondent Abraham Blat.)
The efforts of a few Zionist activists from Zagłębie to obtain a tract of land for Zagłębie Jews are entering the stage of realization and will be crowned with success. This pleasant news was passed on to me on the basis of the minutes of the negotiations of a Zagłębie delegation with the representative of the Jewish Agency, Dr. Fiszel Rotenstreich [?], and it remains only to greet the initiators of this plan, who are giving time and money to this purpose — the initiators, among whom we find the hard-working chairman Mr. Dgiali [?], Mr. Batsha [?], R' Chaim Welner, Mr. Haspel [?], Mr. Jungster and others.
• • •
Dr. Rotenstreich has offered over 500 dunams of land, either near Tiberias or near Magdiel, a colony of Polish Jews. As we are informed, the land at "Magdiel", with water and woodland, is the one under consideration.
The tract lies between the colonies of Ramatayim and Yarkona near Petah Tikva, half an hour's ride by bus from Tel Aviv. The land lies in beautiful surroundings, ringed by Jewish colonies, which is one of the most important things.
During the negotiations with the Jewish Agency the point was stressed that the settled "Zagłębians" will not engage in planting orange groves, but in a mixed intensive farm, which is what comes into consideration here, and today this is one of the most important arguments.
The agronomist Dr. Jagorodski has already worked out a calculation for the farm, which provides for: cows, poultry, beehives, vegetables, etc. According to the plan, 15 dunams of land are reckoned per family, from which one can have a net yearly income of 106 pounds sterling, about 2 thousand 750 Polish złoty. The calculation is reckoned for times that are independent of prosperity.
• • •
Fifty families are foreseen for settlement in the plan of the "Organization of Immigrants from Zagłębie and Silesia", thirty families of them from Palestine and 20 families from Zagłębie.
The sum required of a settling family is 400 pounds. Of this, it is reckoned, 200 pounds will be paid out as small loans from the Keren Kayemet LeIsrael over a number of years, and the remaining 200 pounds are therefore required of the settling family.
However, the "Organization of Zagłębie Immigrants" takes into account the eventuality of less than 200 pounds, believing that the campaign for this purpose in the "fagr" [?] [probably: fund] that is being created will be able to help out those families who do not possess even 200 pounds; and this again depends to a great extent on our Zagłębie capitalists, who will surely understand their duty to stand on guard in the present, so responsible hour, as well as on the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" to urge and rouse the public to fulfil its duty.
The fund being created will have to serve to sustain the idea of settling "Zagłębie" Jews on the soil of the Land of Israel.
It is worth noting that the need for such a "fagr" [?] is felt here at every step for a newly arrived immigrant and even for a resident — this our Zagłębie Jews must remember!
In the short time, 32 families from Sosnowiec, Będzin, Dąbrowa, Königshütte, Zawiercie, Czeladź and other towns have already registered from Palestine for settlement. They have capital and sums of 100 to 1000 pounds; of course, whoever has a larger capital can achieve more, and today a list from Zagłębie is awaited. There is no doubt that there are not a few candidates, and it is the duty of the Zionist and Mizrachi organizations to set up a committee and send the "Zagłębie Organization" in Tel Aviv a list of the candidates.
The list of candidates will be checked by the "Organization" and then sent on to Jerusalem to the Jewish Agency.
• • •
And it seems that all is well and fine. But certificates? — I ask the chairman of the "Zagłębie Organization" — yes, that is a hard nut to obtain, and it will surely not be easy.
• • •
It is further planned, at the expense of the money that will [?] be collected from the settlers to obtain a bank loan, to settle a group of Zagłębie Jews in Jerusalem; but until the plan to settle 50 families is completed, one cannot talk of anything new.
The organization of Zagłębie immigrants is developing and already counts 200 members in Tel Aviv alone (may they multiply), and it believes — the chairman adds — that in the new elections to the Tel Aviv municipal council Zagłębie will have a representative of its own..
Yes, Zagłębie immigrants are organizing. There is a plan for a loan and savings fund and for settlement and other valuable things, and it is our duty to greet these people who are helping somewhat in the matter of "Zagłębie gets land".
In days of a chauvinist wave and zoological antisemitism, such news will surely be a new [?] horizon for our Zagłębie Jews, who, beaten and despised, sit on the hot volcano that spews lava: "Zagłębie".
• • •
And one more piece of news. This week a meeting took place of the "Alumni of the Torah va-Avodah Movement in Zagłębie", regardless of their present party affiliation. 60 men took part in the meeting, and it was resolved to develop a ramified activity in the field of mutual aid, culture, etc. For this purpose a committee was elected, which has set to work immediately.
— Either way, Zagłębie is organizing.
Conference of the Jewish Weekly Press in the Provinces.

On Sunday, at the premises of the Jewish Telegraphic Agency (JTA) in Warsaw, the long-planned conference of the Jewish provincial weeklies took place.
Taking part in the conference were representatives and authorized delegates of 17 weeklies, among them the editors and publishers of the oldest and most popular Jewish weekly papers in the provinces.
After the conference was greeted by the director of the JTA in Poland, editor M. Mozes, a presidium was elected from among the colleagues: Szpigelman (editor of "Zaglembier Tsaytung"), M. Herc (editor of "Radomer Kieltser Lebn") and P. Lauer (editor of "Khelmer Shtime").
In the discussions on how to improve the editorial-journalistic as well as the financial situation of the Jewish provincial press, almost all those present took part, and they unanimously came out in favour of the proposal to create an association of all Jewish weeklies in the provinces and to found an office of the association in Warsaw.
After the lunch break the JTA gave a tea for the delegates, which was also attended by the director of the "Joint" in Poland, Mr. Giterman, who thanked the representatives of the Jewish press for the great interest they show in their papers in the work of "CEKABE" and the "Joint" in general, and for the great assistance they rendered in carrying out the action of the million campaign by "CEKABE" in particular.
Dir. Giterman also expressed his wish to remain in constant, entirely personal contact with the representatives of the provincial press.
After the relevant [?] resolutions had been adopted, the chairman of the conference, Mr. Lejbisz Szpigelman, thanked, in the name of all the delegates, the director of the JTA, editor M. Mozes, as well as the staff of the JTA for their hospitality. Thanks to them the first successful attempt was made to unite the provincial weeklies and thereby also to adopt measures to improve their existence.
To the commission that is to carry out and expand the association, the following colleagues were elected: L. Szpigelman, M. Herc, P. Lauer, A. L. Englender (editor of "Shedletser Vokhnblat"), Orlanski.
With the hope that better times will come for the Jewish newspaper in the provinces, the conference was closed in an elevated mood.
Taking part in the conference were the colleagues: L. Szpigelman (ed. "Zaglembier Tsaytung"), M. Herc (ed. "Radomer Kieltser Lebn"), P. Lauer (ed. "Khelmer Shtime"), A. S. Englender (ed. "Shedletser Vokhnblat"), M. Orlanski (ed. "Byaler Vokhnblat"), Moshe Libfrajnd (ed. "Podlasher Tsaytung"), G. Goldkranc (ed. "Tomashover Vokhnblat"), Tamarzon (ed. "Kalisher Vokh"), A. Orn (ed. "Pruzhaner Shtime"), A. Slucki, ed. "Baranovitsher Vokh", and others.
In conclusion a series of resolutions was adopted, among others, to found an association of the Jewish provincial press and an office with its seat in Warsaw at the JTA.
To the organizing commission of the association were elected Messrs. L. Szpigelman (Będzin), M. Herc (Radom), P. Lauer (Chełm), A. S. Englender (Siedlce), M. Orlanski (Biała Podl.).
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Yitro)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Yitro
—o—
a) "After he had sent her away" (Ex. 18:2)
As long as the people had not been redeemed, Moses renounced family life. At a time when the people languishes in exile, the true leader casts away his own life. Only now, on the threshold of redemption, did Moses take his wife back. Bekhor Shor.
b) "For all the goodness" (ibid., 9)
"The goodness of the manna, the well and the Torah." Mekhilta.
Why precisely these three things, says[?] [the Mekhilta]?
Because of these three things "good" is said. Torah — "For I give you good doctrine; forsake ye not My Torah"; the well — "The Lord bringeth thee into a good land, a land of brooks of water"; manna — "And thou shalt eat and be satisfied, and bless the Lord thy God for the good land". Gresh Karmel.
* * *
"All the goodness" — complete human good, a person's whole well-being, can only exist when he has manna, a well and Torah — food and Torah... When he has only Torah without manna, or manna without Torah, he does not have "all the goodness". Imrei Chen.
c) "That the Lord is greater than all gods" (ibid., 11)
A certain clever Jew, who had converted because of a persecution decree, explained the difference[?] between the Jewish God and other gods:
— When I was a Jew, I did not see my God, but He saw me; today I see my god, and the god does not see me... Don Isaac Abravanel.
d) "And all the people stand by thee" (ibid., 14)
Moses judged the Jews at his own home and did not trouble himself to go to them; therefore he had to go to the Shekhinah. The prophet Samuel, on the other hand, did go to the Jews to judge them and did not wait until the Jews would come to him — so he merited[?] that the Shekhinah came to him... Midrash.
e) "Because the people come unto me to inquire of God... when they have a matter, it cometh unto me" (ibid., 15)
When it is a matter that concerns piety, kashrut and the like — "the people come unto me to inquire of God" — then the people come in masses; "and when they have a matter" — when, however, it concerns some [?] affair, money matters — "it cometh unto me" — only one comes to me: the party concerned[?]. Duda'ei Maharai.
f) "Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob" (19:3)
"Thus shalt thou say — in the Holy Tongue. To the house of Jacob — these are the women." Midrash.
The time had come for Moses to speak the Holy Tongue even to the women, since even when the Jews had already left Egypt, the women were probably still flirting with the Yiddish language... Leket Amarim.
* * *
Therefore the Blessed Name commanded Moses to give the Torah first to the women, because the law is: "If one bought from the husband and then bought again from the wife, the purchase is void, for she says: I did it to please my husband"; the woman acts[?] according to what the husband wants and not by her own will; therefore God commanded to tell them the Torah first... Beit HaLevi.
g) "The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai" (ibid., 23)
For had the Jews gone up Mount Sinai, they would have grown so great in their own eyes, they would have become such arrogant people, that they would no longer have been worthy of the Torah...
Only Moses could go up to the Almighty, as it were, on Mount Sinai and still remain "the meekest of all men". "Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place?" — that was Moses. He ascended the mountain of the Lord, Mount Sinai, "and stood in His holy place", and yet he did not grow great in his own eyes. He remained on one and the same level in his own eyes. R. Pinchas HaLevi Horowitz.
h) "Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be long" (20:12)
For every commandment one is rewarded measure for measure; so with what can one reward him who honours his parents? Honour is, after all, a thing one must deserve, and not everyone deserves honour.
To this the Torah says "that thy days may be long". Your reward will be that you will live long, and he who lives long becomes an old man, and he is honoured even when he is an ignoramus and has deserved nothing at all... Pirchei Shoshanim.
i) "Thou shalt not steal" (ibid., 13)
The Torah says simply "Thou shalt not steal": you may not steal any money, nor any souls, nor deceive people's minds, nor deceive the mind of the Most High... Commentary of the Shakh on the Torah.
* * *
The Maggid of Kozienice used to say:
He who merely says that he fasts from Sabbath to Sabbath, while at home he eats and drinks, only deceives people's minds; he who actually fasts from Sabbath to Sabbath and thinks that he is doing the Master of the Universe who knows what favour — he deceives the mind of the Most High... Pesher Irot[?].
For the "Keren Hayesod" Campaign in Będzin / The Holy Unrest / Foundation of Foundations!

[Będzin — the Keren Hayesod campaign; a campaign article and a feuilleton.]
[Banner across the top of the page:] For the "Keren Hayesod" Campaign in Będzin.
The Holy Unrest.
Bete Landber
I.
Once again we come to you, Jews of Zagłębie, on the mission of the "Keren Hayesod", to demand of you the tax for the Jewish "state enterprise", for the Land of Israel that is building itself. In our educational work on the importance of the "Keren Hayesod" we always used to rely on the familiar argument of the sad reality of exile. We regularly awakened Jewish consciousness, pointed to the insecure fate of the Jewish people in the lands of exile, to the terrible economic and political situation of the Jewish communities in the East European countries, where the antisemitic waves rage more and more. The pauperization of the Jewish masses becomes more catastrophic from day to day, and in the last two years yet another bloody link has been added to the long chain of Jewish pain and suffering; into the eternal "cup of the exiles" [?] has fallen yet another bitter drop: the tragedy of German Jewry. In the very heart of West European culture was born the wild madness of "racial antisemitism", in the terrible, gruesome forms of the "Nuremberg laws", which remind us of the times of barbarism. The extermination policy of the Third Reich is conducted in the simplest, most literal sense of "to destroy, to slay and to annihilate all the Jews".
In view of all these sad phenomena, which have provoked panic and a mood of despair among the Jewish masses, we regularly awakened, encouraged and comforted the tormented Jewish people with the well-known prophetic words of consolation, "Comfort ye, comfort ye my people"; with the strength of this faith we proudly unfurled the blue-white flag, which called for self-liberation, for creating a home of our own in the old-new Zion-home. Hard was the road of the "birth pangs of redemption"; we had to wage a stubborn struggle with the various enemies within and without, but the will to survive of the Jewish nation overcame all difficulties, and today we already have the privilege of seeing "the beginning of redemption". The contours of the Jewish national home are becoming ever more distinct, and thanks to the national funds, Keren Kayemeth LeIsrael and Keren Hayesod, we have succeeded in taking in Palestine the very most important positions of state significance, such as, for example, the school and health systems, Rutenberg's electrification of the Jordan, the revival of the Dead Sea through the founding of the Novomeysky company to exploit its rich mineral treasures, the afforestation [?] of large areas at various points of the Jewish settlement in Palestine.
Must we this year too, in carrying out the Keren Hayesod campaign, make use of all the arguments mentioned above? Must we, in today's tragic situation too, when the red-hot rods [?] fall on our shoulders, lash us and drive us into a panic-stricken exodus wherever our eyes may lead, still explain the important significance of the Land of Israel for the tormented Jewish people? No and no! Superfluous are the words, superfluous the agitation; the time for immediate deeds has come, there is no time for various calculations. One must not [?] hesitate now, when the danger is great; and when we find it necessary at the present moment to speak nevertheless of the great importance of the "Keren Hayesod", we no longer do so in view of the tragic reality of exile, which no longer requires any arguments of persuasion; rather, we do it now as a consequence of the present Palestinian reality, which at this moment demands a certain enlightenment among the broad Jewish masses.
II.
The situation in Palestine demands of us enormous vigilance and responsibility. We now face in Palestine two important, serious phenomena of two distinct characters, one economic-internal and the other political-external, which may have a decisive significance for the fate of the further development of the upbuilding of Palestine.
The project of creating a Legislative Council in Palestine is without doubt one of the greatest dangers, one that may threaten the whole foundation of our upbuilding of the land; even if the two most important problems, immigration and land purchase, should be eliminated from the competences of the Legislative Council and remain subject to the decision of the High Commissioner, there still remains the danger that the Legislative Council will be used by the Arabs as a high [?] tribune for their national-chauvinist slogans, and they will always strive to harm Jewish interests; and who knows whether the Palestine government will always be able to withstand the constant pressure from the Arab extremists and not be forced to give them various concessions at the expense of Jewish interests. And therefore it is no wonder that the whole of world Jewry, from left to right, has united in order to protest jointly against the violation of the Balfour Declaration, which is in contradiction to the content of the Palestine Mandate. The present Executive has been put to a great trial in this so difficult defensive struggle. We believe and hope that the Zionist Executive, with President Weizmann at its head, will succeed in passing the trial by fire honourably; in any case we must be clear that the power of decision does not lie in the hands of the people; we can only show our strong passive resistance, but in this case the decision will rest with the external political factors, on which we do not have enough power to exert influence towards a radical change — in this particular respect.
Quite different is the second, economic-internal phenomenon of today's Yishuv. A break has come in the "prosperity" that prevailed until now; there is something of a crisis in Palestine, with several thousand unemployed; the number of certificates of the delayed October schedule has been [?] considerably [?] reduced; immigration is slowing down, and this of course again affects the Palestinian economy: the inflow of capital is shrinking, the building movement and industrial development are somewhat [?] checked, etc. [?]; memories float up [?] upside down, in reflections of the years 1926/27. Today [?] too there is already a small number of "returnees". And precisely in view of this depressed condition we must all the more explain the important significance of the national capitals as a means of defence against the various forms of crisis. When the "Keren Hayesod" celebrated its 15th jubilee a few months ago, and among the many greetings I also read the warm greeting of Sir Wyndham Deedes, I recalled his words, spoken in 1927 during his visit to Poland: "All the Jewish communities in the world will set their little clocks by the clock of the Land of Israel". Like a prophet's his profound words ring today; it took a great measure of foresight to be able to assert in January 1927, at the time of the greatest crisis in Palestine, that the life of all Jewish communities would be shaped according to the course and tempo of Palestine's development. Today, when we see that his prophecy has almost been fulfilled, we can quite boldly correct the slogan into the formula: "If all the Jewish little clocks are set by the Palestine clock, then the 'Keren Hayesod' is the spindle [?] of the great Palestine clock, which sets in motion all the other little wheels of the clock". If there was ever once a contested question about "private capital" and "national capital", now the present moment has come, which may rightly be called — in President Weizmann's expression of 1926 — a moment of "holy unrest", which confirms again the correct diagnosis we have always made: that private capital will never be a special means of protection against various economic shocks. Private capital will always seek favourable conjunctures, and in a bad conjuncture it will withdraw entirely; national capital, by contrast, goes, just like the pioneer, to the hardest positions and paves the way for private capital that comes later. Therefore, at this present responsible moment, we must exert all our strength to reinforce the financial apparatus of the upbuilding of Palestine, the "Keren Hayesod", which must intervene with its funds in all economic fields and energetically undertake the rehabilitation of the unsound economic policy that has been pursued until now. The great disproportion between town and village must be reduced by every means; the slogan must be "face to the village"; we must, as far as possible, start again the real Zionist settlement work, which in recent years has been greatly neglected. We too were dragged into the "prosperity round-dance", and we must sober up from the intoxication; and if averting [?] the danger in the external political field does not lie entirely in our hands, then averting [?] the second, internal economic danger depends solely and exclusively on ourselves. The key to the question lies in our own hands, and if we succeed in removing the economic danger, it will be much easier for us to fight, to be capable of resisting the threatening political danger. We believe that the Jewish people will know how to appreciate the present responsible moment and will be ready for the heavy financial sacrifices in order to reinforce the national funds. Imbued with this deep faith, we set about carrying out this year's "Keren Hayesod" campaign, which must be crowned with the greatest success. That is the command of the hour.
—o—
Foundation of Foundations! (Feuilleton)
Dr. B. Feld [?]
The foundation of the "Keren Hayesod" (Foundation Fund) is water. Water — the life of man and beast; water — the blessing of field and plant; water — the most necessary thing for every creature.
The whole world, actually, rests on water. The "Keren Hayesod" with its strength struck water from the rock (drilling), drew the sap out of the dried-up veins of the aged, neglected mother earth, and thereby struck roots in her.
City dwellers, who draw water from the wall, know only from reading what great importance water has in the desert — just like wine in a settlement. The Jewish pioneers who penetrated into the wastelands of the Land of Israel to till and fructify [?] them felt the lack of water deep in their bones. It lacked them a soul; they moistened the earth with their sweat, gladly gave their blood for her —
But blood is not water...
They indeed wanted with all their heart to put their hands into water — but it was not the ritual washing of hands...
For the purchased tracts of land one absolutely had to create the conditions of life, of existence. The first thing of all — water.
This task the "Keren Hayesod" took upon itself and fulfilled it completely, in full measure.
The "Keren Hayesod" was the Prince of Water, who with the golden key forged from donated Jewish coins opened the locked treasury [?] of the earth, and she again gave birth to water.
Indeed the flourishing settlements of Palestine today confirm it. They are the great truth that has come up, like olive oil on top of the water.
Now, when people flee [?] from the fire of exile, they already meet water in the colonies; the water gushes and people's spirits [?] rejoice; one marvels — from whose hands was this gift handed, who brought the moisture into the hard life.
One knows that —
this source of life, the greatness of the wells' abundance, the drawing of water with joy — all this was brought about by the "Keren Hayesod".
The spirit of the "Keren Hayesod" hovers over the face of the water.
So, in the beginning the foundation was water. The water gave nourishment to the dry land. The wild springs were glimpsed [?], from which the further acquisitions extended. Later everything was already built on water (not bad at all).
It is "waters without end"...
In this water drowned all the talk of the haters of Zion, and all stumbling-blocks were flooded.
And the water-canal stretches from the Jewish settlements, from towns and townlets — from everywhere, where people even helped to grease the iron, to dig and discover the deep secret of water that the earth had hidden in her entrails.
All Jews who pay the voluntary tax, the water levy, have a share in it.
But the role of the "water-carriers" is still far from finished; fresh soil keeps coming, thirsty for water, and it must be watered, made fit for sowing and planting.
The spring of the "Keren Hayesod" must not dry up for a single moment, for it is the breast that suckles, with a mother's devotion, all the newborn settlements.
"For the sake of N. [?] thou shalt not spare any water".
The more water for our exhausted land, the more refreshment and nourishment. Thanks to that the great voice will rise up [?] over the water — the heralding voice!...

Such Luck He Has.

[Humour — poem.] (From the series "Jewish Fortunes").
1.
Leyver is a craftsman.
Ever since he became engaged,
all the time, he says, there has been
no livelihood at all:
such luck he has,
the Jew, the craftsman —
instead of having work
he has, of all things — a family,
and the wife is a cursed one [?]:
we want [?] — she shouts — to eat!
But one is, after all, a human being,
one can sometimes forget.
2.
Leyver goes from village to village.
He gets up at the crack of dawn —
he looks for work, whatever there is,
just to earn something.
3.
Whatever you take him for, Leyver is good for it,
he is an expert at everything,
above all he is good for that —
for which all men are good...
4.
So Leyver goes along,
abashed [?] and lost in thought,
and wonders where one finds work now,
though it is already evening.
5.
And the wife cries with the children,
little tiny lads —
they all sit and look out
for the husband, for the father...
6.
Meanwhile night falls outside,
the stars already twinkle —
he hurries into the synagogue
to hear Kedushah and Barkhu...
7.
Leyver has been a craftsman
for forty years already —
ask whether, apart from a family,
he has saved anything?
M. Grinszpan.

Special Universities for Jews.
[Humour — satire.] As we have learned, the Endeks [the Polish National Democrats] intend to open special universities for the Jewish academics, where the following sciences will be taught:
The art of knitting — braiding tzitzit.
Surgery — circumcision.
Architecture — building sukkahs.
Zoology — swinging kapparot.
Astronomy — blessing the new moon.
Sport — swimming in the mikveh.
Chatskele Kalbonis on Anti-Jewish Terror.

[Humour — satire in a mock Galician vernacular, monologue.] Tell me, lads, do you read the dispatches [?] from Abyssinia? What ... [?] is in it? "Sumelini" [Mussolini] slaps himself on the belly, ... A Question (Kushye).

(A motif of the times)
Master of the Universe, Master of the Universe,
hear what a question your golem has,
a golem, the golem of all golems,
whom You created, You, Life of the Worlds.
You gave us golems signs
of the Messiah's coming at the End of Days.
The End of Days — it has come;
why then are the shofars still silent and mute?
You gave us a good promise:
the Messiah will come when not a penny (pruta)
will anyone have, and no one will possess,
and insolence (chutzpah) will rule on roads and paths.
Well, what a coin looks like we have already forgotten;
impudence and chutzpah are now the princesses,
the two of them dominate and govern your little world,
knocking at the windows, knocking at the doors.
Whoever is not insolent is surely in trouble;
insolent men and insolent women are now the authorities;
the hints and signs have been fulfilled —
a time such as never was: it is the End of Days!
So where is your 'poor one' (ani), your dear messenger,
who rides upon the donkey — I mean, the Messiah!
Master of the Universe! I say it into Your ear:
it is all upside down, it is all upside down!...
A. Kerem.

— I will guard you like the apple of my eye, and so that you will not be bored in the hours when I am busy, and knowing your kind little heart, I will give you an occupation.
— What do you mean, you are going to engage me for another post? — she laughed and stroked his cheeks.
— Yes, dear, I would not entrust such an important post to anyone as to you. Do you know why? Because God created you only to do good for mankind; that is why I want to hand over to you the work, which you will surely do with pleasure.
— Let me hear already what kind of occupation you are going to give me; you are making me curious?
— Three times a week I go to visit the old people who are in our old-age home, which I have already greatly improved. It is a very important institution, my dear, in which one cannot rely on the servants. Every person prays to God not to abandon him in old age, when he can no longer help himself; therefore we must help him, because that is our duty — we too will some day become old people. Each time [someone] from our office[?] goes with me, and now, my dear, I want to lay on you the duty of standing in for me. You, my dear, with your keen[?] eye and your kind heart, will be better suited as overseer of the old people. You will surely find out what they lack and what they need.
— My dear friend, I am proud that you hand me such an important task, which I will fulfil with my best conscience — she smiled.
— I am sure of that, my dear, that you will do more for them than I. But I have one more request of you. Two days ago I was there myself, and in the twelfth room I found a new resident, whom they had brought in from the street. For three days already he has done nothing but sleep. But imagine, from the first moment I saw him I could not tear my eyes away from him; something drew me to him, a secret, incomprehensible force, and I stood a long time by his bed, believing that he would wake from his deep sleep.
— Who brought him there?
— As I was informed, he came to our office here[?], and when the maid explained to him that he [the master] had gone away for two weeks, he collapsed, began to scream and weep [printed 'veybn'] that he was lost. The maid took fright, called Mister[?] Bleier, and he brought him to the old-age home. A great pity seized me for this unfortunate man, who has surely lived through a hard tragedy and sought calm in the White Sea [sic]. That is how it is, my dear — man lives through many tragedies in his short life — he sighed heavily.
— Moses[?], you must forgive me for my question. But I swear to you by our holy love that I harbour no suspicion at all, apart from the curiosity to know it; and since, as you have just said, man lives through many tragedies in his short life, I ask you to explain to me what was the reason for your terrible change when Mr. Green showed you the photograph of his acquaintance?
A shudder passed over his body and he let his head fall on his chest.
— I feel, Moses[?], that you are hiding from me a great tragedy of your life. Do you believe that is right of you?
— No, my dear. I hide nothing from you, because the tragedy of my mother and of me is well known to you. I told you everything about my father, how he abandoned my mother and me and married another woman; and imagine, my dear, how astonished I was when in the picture that Mr. Green showed us I recognised none other than my father's wife, who was called Balbina. That same Balbina is now Mr. Green's lady friend, who — as he told me on the ship — snatched my father away and lived with him more than a year.
— Had my mother not been in the compartment, I would have told you the tragedy at once. But you understand that I could not do it in her presence. Only, as I gathered from Mr. Green, my father lived through a great life-tragedy in the short time he lived with his second wife.
— Come, children, have lunch — they heard Chanele's[?] voice as she entered the room.

The "Ne'ilah" Session on the Kehilla Budget

[Będzin — kehilla.] On Sunday the kehilla council held a session at which the kehilla budget was adopted in third reading.
A Sabbath-like [?] mood reigned at the session. Only 6 councillors were present, all of them from the national camp, and they listened to the lament of the chairman, Mr. Landner. "One's heart — he says — can simply burst from the web of intrigues and slanders. [Unclear words] incited [?] against me, but the side that has a large share in what hurts Mr. L. so much is absent, and his words ring out — like a voice crying in the wilderness..."
Before proceeding to the "historic" [?] budget items, the chairman relates that the "Agudah" councillors, Messrs. Szenberg, Riński, Fiszel and Erlich, filed a complaint against him with the starosta [district head]. The complaint states that "Mr. Landner knowingly falsifies the minutes of the council sessions and in general is not fit to hold the office of president of the council."
The practical result of the complaint is — says Mr. L. — that 3 days after the complaint was submitted, the starosta had already ordered that elections for a president of the council be held by the 20th of this month.
President Mr. Rubinlicht points out in his reply that the board had received the demand concerning the election of the president several days earlier, before the Agudah complaint was filed.
Taking part in the discussion on this matter were Herszlowicz, Kornfeld and others, and on the chairman's proposal all the remaining budget items were adopted without any discussion, according to a draft [?] of the board.

An Oath by Black Candles in the Jędrzejów Beit Midrash.
Last Friday in the Jędrzejów beit midrash, in the presence of the lawyers Jan[?] Jaczkowski[?] and Tysławicz[?], a delegate of the rabbinate and a large crowd of Jews, Mrs. P. A festive welcome in honour of Rabbi Gold

On Wednesday the president of the world „Mizrachi“ organisation, Rabbi Gold, stayed in Kielce. At the railway station the honoured guest was met by the Mizrachi committee, the representatives of the Mizrachi youth organisations and ordinary people.
In the evening the lecture took place in the Teatr Polski.
After a cordial[?] speech of welcome by Mr. Yoshie[?] Bekerman, Rabbi Gold, amid a storm of applause from a crowd of a thousand, began his masterly lecture.
In a lecture of nearly three hours the speaker discussed the economic, spiritual and political situation in Zionism. The speaker dwelt at length on the planned Legislative Council and stressed with satisfaction the full unanimity that prevails in the whole Yishuv and in all of Jewry regarding the Legislative Council.
True — says Rabbi Gold — there is now a crisis in Eretz Israel, but in the Diaspora countries this crisis is greatly exaggerated; it is a lower Garden of Eden compared with the bitter economic and political situation of the Jews in the Diaspora countries. The Jewish Yishuv in Eretz Israel is firmly rooted in the land and no storm wind[?] is able to tear it down. What prevails[?] is merely an inflated crisis, and it will and must soon disappear.
At the present very serious moment the whole Jewish people must be firmly cemented together and, with united forces, help the Executive in its hard struggle. Everyone must now place himself in the service of Zionism; the Hasidim too must put into practice the Rebbes' ruling concerning Eretz Israel, and must make the greatest efforts to strengthen the Zionist funds, the Keren Kayemet and the Keren Hayesod.
Rabbi Gold also discusses the religious questions in Eretz Israel and explains that the religious postulates of „Mizrachi“ are being realised step by step, but we remain on guard that the Congress decisions on Sabbath observance be carried out in full.
Rabbi Gold's lecture was heard with the greatest attention, was rewarded with loud ovations and closed with a protest resolution against the Legislative Council and the singing of „Hatikvah“.
Afterwards a festive banquet in honour of the guest was held at the Mizrachi club, and in a very congenial Eretz-Israel mood the assembled public spent the time at finely laid tables until dawn.
Rabbi Gold's visit left an unforgettable impression on the entire Jewish population.

[Częstochowa — antisemitism, boycott and community.] (From our correspondent A. Wrocławski)
Conference of the kehillas of the Częstochowa district (powiat).
On the initiative of the kehilla president Mr. Rozenberg, a conference was held on Sunday in the gmina (municipal) hall, attended by representatives of the surrounding kehillas.
The representatives of the small surrounding towns reported on the situation of the Jews in their places.
The delegates from Truskolasy report on the dreadful material situation of the Jews there. A strong boycott campaign is being waged; the Jewish traders in the countryside are pelted with stones and have to hide until they get police help.
If it is noticed that a Christian goes in to buy from a Jew, he is threatened[?], and there was even a case of a Christian who had bought from a Jew being badly beaten and having his windowpanes smashed.
The same lamentations are heard from the Jews of Mushistan[?] (unidentified place), Krzepice and elsewhere. The situation in the public (state) schools has also become unbearable: the Jewish children are beaten in the schools themselves, and on the way back from school they are attacked.
In Kłobuck the boycott campaign is taking ever sharper forms. A Christian who buys from a Jew has a slip[?] pinned[?] on his back with the inscription "Ta świnia kupiła u Żyda" ("This swine bought from a Jew"), and the buyer is escorted with stones as he goes home.
Thus the Jews unburdened their hearts and told of their troubles and fears, their torments and their dread of tomorrow.
After a lengthy exchange of views a series of resolutions was adopted, among them to join a relief campaign for the starving Jews in all the small towns.

Yellow headlight beams can prevent car accidents

[Science and technology — traffic.] One of the most famous researchers among the French motorists, Mr. Baudry de Saunier[?], has published a brochure discussing the advantages of introducing yellow lighting in car headlights.
The French Ministry of the Interior took an interest in the matter and handed the detailed investigation of it to a special commission composed of the most respected motorists in France.
Not long ago this commission published a report which fully confirms the arguments of the author of the brochure, and it turned out that introducing yellow lighting in motor traffic is absolutely expedient, because it does not irritate the eye and one sees better and faster. It was confirmed that two cars can avoid a disaster even with the full beams of their headlights.
On the basis of the commission's findings, the French Ministry of the Interior has ordered that from 1 July (lipiec) 1936 yellow lights must without fail be introduced in the motor traffic running on the public roads.

[Upper Silesia — community and rabbinate.] At the last joint meeting of the above-mentioned governing bodies, the only matter dealt with was the topical issue, namely the extension of the Piłsudski decree [the 1927 decree on Jewish religious communities] to the Silesian kehillas.
Rabbi Chameides, in a lengthy and detailed lecture, diligently[?] treated kehilla autonomy from the historical point of view and as the matter stands today, presenting the situation in the individual Silesian kehillas, where there are[?] often representatives of the various Polish regions with opposing opinions and views on Jewish life, and the role of the rabbi, the spiritual leader, in uniting them and bringing them to harmonious cooperation.
The esteemed speaker drew in his logical exposition on very rich material and showed much knowledge and learning on the problem under discussion.
After the lecture an exhaustive discussion developed, in which almost all those present took part.
A compromise proposal was then adopted unanimously, namely: 1) not to press for the extension of the Piłsudski decree to the Silesian kehillas, and 2) the rabbinate will be represented at the meetings of the kehilla board.

Small Remarks on Big Matters.

In a Time When "All May Slaughter"...
In the country, it turns out, everything is in the best of order. There is no unemployment, trade is flourishing, industry is developing, business is prospering, the state budget has a surplus — in short, all is fine and dandy with us. Were it not so, the deputies of the Polish Sejm would surely have other worries on their minds than choosing an easy death for the cattle..
And that really is a worry! Some trifle [lit. "one trifle"]; after all, we have already reached the point in our country where people take such care of the beast and of its sufferings at slaughter.
For the living creature itself, however, this is probably a slim difference; and some say that death from the sharp ḥalaf [slaughtering knife] is quicker and better than the dull death of stunning.
Less suffering, and got off more cheaply.
In our times that too is a bit of consolation.
—
In the matter of Jewish shechita and of slaughters of Jews, we have 2 systems: one pass of the ḥalaf across the throat and the account is settled. Our Endeks [National Democrats] think very highly of this kind of slaughter of Jews — they watch greedily for every moment when they will be able to set the Nazi methods going.
But there is one more system, which is called: S-T-U-N-N-I-N-G. And this means was seized upon here even before the director of the Sejm chancellery agreed to publish the exact details of Madame Prystor's [Janina Prystorowa] shechita bill.
And what does it mean to stun a living creature? First you take the piece of bread out of its mouth, you push it out of everywhere, you drive it from place to place, you beat it, you flog it and you do not let it catch its breath. That is a death with torments and tortures, that is a state in which one is led to the slaughter and does not know when the end will finally come.
Madame Prystor is apparently a soft-hearted and kind-hearted woman; she cannot, poor thing, watch the ḥalaf swinging over the Jewish cattle; she wants them, the cattle, to be stunned first...
That is more refined and nicer, without the squealing[?] and screaming — and the same goal is achieved.
As long as the little Jews suffer and perish like beasts — Madame Prystor surely means it for their good..
—
And very original she is not, Madame Prystor, after all. And her method of slaughter certainly, certainly not. Incidentally: can anyone in our times invent anything original in this field — — —
— It is, after all, a time of "all may slaughter"...
N. S.
—o—
Jewish Labour, Too, Is in Exile.
Much ink [lit. "many inkwells"] has already been poured out, many pens broken and a mountain of articles written about[?] the Jewish employers who do not want to employ any Jewish workers. But to this day the matter has not been favourably resolved, and Jewish working people wander about in their tens of thousands without work.
Ask a Jewish factory owner why he does not employ Jewish workers, and he shakes out, as if from his sleeve, a flood of excuses.
They hold a firm belief that the gentile worker is more honest and more loyal than the Jewish one, and against[?] a belief no fight helps — only enlightenment.
One ought to explain to all these kinds of Jewish employers that, as regards honesty, loyalty and ability, the Jewish worker is in no way inferior to the gentile, and that it pays a Jewish employer better to employ precisely Jewish workers.
That a Jewish worker is capable and does good work, nobody has ever yet doubted.
The Jewish employers who do not employ any Jewish workers are perhaps rather poorly educated. But they have, it seems, heard an old joke which they cannot forget.
— Why are the people of Egypt black? — someone asked, and the answer is:
— They were blackened because they employed Jewish workers in building Pithom and Raamses.
And from many Jewish employers you hear the same refrain: they do not want to be blackened, they say, and they want no Jewish workers.
And all the other complaints against the Jewish worker have no substance whatever; they are taken from the antisemites.
But all this must be explained to those Jewish factory owners, so that they understand the mistake they have made until now.
For in truth they are no antisemites, these Jewish factory owners who do not let a single Jewish worker cross their threshold; they may well be synagogue gabbaim, leaders of Jewish organizations and honour-seekers among Jews — but at bottom they are no businessmen, even though they may be rich: they do not know that the Jewish worker, with his energy, ambition and honesty, is precisely a blessing and good fortune for them.
And that is what they must be taught.
R.
—o—
The Jewish Hospital in Sosnowiec.
In the last issue of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" we read the appeal to the Jewish population of Zagłębie to support the Jewish hospital in Sosnowiec. This appeal was addressed in particular to the women of Sosnowiec, Dąbrowa and Zawiercie, the towns from which the hospital often has patients. The purpose of the appeal is that committees be formed which, following the example of Będzin, will collect first of all linen. The Będzin committee deserves recognition for the initiative, which should bring good success, for it is almost certain that no kind-hearted woman will refuse it, especially since it is for poor Jewish patients who often come to the hospital without so much as a shirt on their backs.
As is well known, the Jewish hospital in Sosnowiec was founded before the World War by a group of kind-hearted people. Those who wanted to ease the pains of the Jewish patient created the hospital; besides that there were many people who visited the patient, very often spent the night at his side, and more than one patient, on leaving the hospital — also received material support — and today..
Today the hospital stands abandoned; rarely does anyone so much as mention it, as though it were not an indispensable institution, a matter of life; one neither hears nor sees anyone donating a larger sum of money to the hospital. Jewish society, too, is passive; not a single event ["impreza"] is organized that would yield a significant income, with which one could renovate the operating room, the dressing room, the doors and windows; and outside a nicer fence ["parkan"] and a better aesthetic appearance are badly needed.
Today's crisis cannot serve as an excuse; with good will no one will refuse — neither money nor goods — for the benefit of the Jewish hospital in Sosnowiec, for it is the only place for the poor Jewish patient in the present time.
H. Szer.
The "Kest" Is Over!... (Monologue of an Amnestied Man)

[Humour and satire — monologue; Będzin.]
Y. Operzhanek [?]
— Where do I come from?
— From the yeshiva I come.
— From which yeshiva?
— From the Będzin yeshiva on Okrzei Street.
— Why was I sitting? Because of a trifle, because of a mistake: because of the Havdalah. Instead of on Saturday night, I said "borei me'orei ha-esh" on a plain Wednesday...
So they started in on me [lit. "took me on the cymbal"]:
— Is it possible? How does one make "Havdalah" in the middle of the week?
— A mistake, I made, I say, I made a mistake, well, what's all the fuss? What do I get for it?
— Three little years — they answered me.
Well, so because of that "mistake" I did sit out [?] two and a half years in the "yeshiva" on Okrzei.
So listen, Jews, how good I had it there — after all, I "sat in greatness"! Only then did I know what life is; I had real "odpoczynek" [rest], I "enjoyed" [?; Polish używać] a good life — whoever grants me even a morsel of good — all kinds of good friends, my neighbour, the landlord, the mother-in-law and other "good friends" — I wish them just such a bit of "worldly pleasure" [olam ha-zeh].
What did I lack? The finest and the best, a star [?] from the sky they gave me; I had the "lower Garden of Eden".
I ate "pension" according to the "menu", as in a "Lechbril" [?] boarding-house.
I slept "wygodnie" [comfortably] — as [?] in the Grand Hotel... And then the supervision! They "guarded" me like a precious stone, never took an eye off me; at every step they watched over me like an only son, never once did they leave me alone; I always had an "escort"; they "kept me company" [?; Polish towarzyszyć] and "entertained" me [Polish bawić].
And then the "towarzystwo" [company]! Do you know what "dobre towarzystwo" [good company] I had: the very "śmietanka" [cream], scholars, geniuses, artists, "prominent personalities", men of the world, the very "aristocracy"; if you don't believe me, I'll introduce them to you.
Zerakhl Cechowiec [the "guildsman"]
A guild-certified master, by trade an upholsterer: he "felt about" and "pulled".
Hershl the Photographer
A first-rate professional: whatever he sees, he "snaps": clothes from a corridor, laundry from attics, a bundle of goods from a cart — a specialist in his trade.
Vove the Artist
A lad with first-rate abilities: what the eyes see, the hands take — a "zdolny" [talented] little fellow.
The "Operator"
He does not operate on appendixes [Polish ślepa kiszka], not on [?], not on gallstones; he "operates" in the bank, on the train, "frequents" the richest houses — an "osobistość" [personage].
The "Bramkarz" [goalkeeper]
A lad with an earring, a first-rate "sportowiec" [sportsman]. Not a member of "Hakoah", not of "Maccabi", yet he is a good "goalkeeper": he always scores right into the "gate". Besides that he is a great sage; on his tombstone will be engraved "With wisdom he opens gates."
The "Exporter"
A dear little man, a golden soul, a respected merchant, a "hurtownik" [wholesaler] of live "kurczaki" [chickens]. His "head office" he keeps in "Buzhine" [?], besides branches. Makes huge "obroty" [turnovers]. A "branżysta" [trade expert] of the "first sort".
Joint-Stock Co. G. G. R.
Do you know who this is? A director of the local joint-stock company G. G. R.
— What, you don't know the [?] "spółka akcyjna" [joint-stock company]? How should you know? But had you been in the "yeshiva" on Okrzei, you would have known that the initials G. G. R. stand for geneyve, gzeyle, retsikhe [theft, robbery, murder].
So I have the honour of introducing to you the director of the Joint-Stock Co. G. G. R., and now you know what kind of "śmietanka" I had to do with, who my "towarzystwo" was.
Well, I ask you, what did I lack? I had it as good as could be, since I had "dobre towarzystwo", I ate "pension" by the menu, I slept "comfortably" as in the Grand Hotel, they guarded me like an only son, and besides that I was protected from creditors, sequestrators, blows and calamities. In front of the door I had a guard standing with a gun in his hand, and if a creditor with a little protested bill had tried to barge in on me — he would not have been sure of his life... A splendid [?] life I had in the Będzin "yeshiva".
Now it is bitter — did I need an amnesty? For what misery? The moment I came out free, they started without letup giving me "sholem aleykhem".
— Sholem aleykhem, what's happening with the protested bill?
— Sholem aleykhem, Reb Sender, what will be with the rent?
— Sholem aleykhem, in-law, what will be with the dowry?
— Sholem aleykhem, daddy dear, what will be with a little winter coat?
— Sholem aleykhem, my partner [lit. "my team-mate"], when will you redeem the sealskin [?] fur from the pawnshop?
— "Dzień dobry" [good morning], "nakaz płatniczy" [payment order].
— "Dzień dobry", "zaległy podatek" [tax arrears].
Endless sholem-aleykhems and dzień-dobrys, one "teka" [briefcase] out and a second "teka" in; I don't know what is happening to me. I am already worn out [?] by the sholem-aleykhems and by the dzień-dobrys. For three years I had peace, I didn't hear my wife's well-known little tune: "Może masz?" [maybe you have (some money)?], for three years I saw no "teka" before my eyes, and suddenly — here you are, an amnesty. An amnesty on my head — who needed it, who? How good I had it when I went about in the grey underwear with the little cap on my head, when I had a free flat, a free pension, when a guard stood before the door with a gun in his hand and didn't let the creditors near me. Where does one find such a guard for the door today?...
The worst thing is that I don't recognise anyone.
Three years ago my wife was a "ciemna szatynka" [dark brunette], and now she is a "jasna blondynka" [light blonde]. My eldest daughter has, in the course of the three years... become ten years younger. My janitor [stróż] Walenty, who three years ago knew no more than three things: spraying, sweeping and "pijaństwo" [drunkenness], has become a "Jew-expert" and writes articles in the "Kurier Zachodni".
Stasiek the pigeon-thief wears a student cap, carries a thick stick in his hand, and it doesn't suit him to sit on the same bench with the "Żydzi".
At the market a season has come, and they "tear" goods out of people's hands.
Altogether three years — and how everything has changed. Had I stayed on in the "yeshiva", I wouldn't have known about all these troubles. I would still be on "kest" [free board] today.
An amnesty on my head!
Memories of the First Zionists in Zagłębie

By Gershon Stawski.
The first Zionist society in Zagłębie was founded in the year 1898 in Sosnowiec. Its chief founder was the well-known national poet H. N. Bialik, of blessed memory. Some time later a society was also founded in Będzin. For the sake of organising the Będzin branch we used to travel to Będzin several times in a row, every Shabbat evening, where, on the New Market, in the house that belonged to Kalman Langer, was the first Zionist minyan. There we used to meet with the Będzin Zionists, and various Zionist problems and organisational questions would be discussed. R' Berish Preger, of blessed memory, liked to give a short sermon every Shabbat evening, linking Zionist questions with the weekly Torah portion.
The first Będzin Zionists were: Preger, Wilbuszewicz, Wrancberg[?], Frenkel, Wodawiński[?] and others.
The first Zionists in Sosnowiec were Lithuanian Jews who lived in Sosnowiec at the time. Our leader Bialik used to demand of me and of one more of the founders, R' Yaakov Weinberg, that we draw the assimilationists into our movement. Bialik used to say that the Hasidim and the middle class we would not lose, because sooner or later they must come to us. But the assimilationists we must recruit as early as possible, because afterwards it would be too late.
At that time Sosnowiec had the largest and most important assimilationist colony — even compared with such centres as Warsaw and Łódź. Strolling with Bialik one summer evening that year along the main street of Sosnowiec, we were met by one of the oldest and most cultivated assimilationists that Sosnowiec possessed, and he greeted me. This was the then forwarding agent Kampiński, a convinced, conscious assimilationist of many generations' standing. He came from an assimilated family from Greater Poland; an older brother or uncle of his, Kampiński, had also held a senior post in General Dąbrowski's army. The Sosnowiec Kampiński, too, had taken part in the uprising (powstanie) of 1862; his dress was genuinely national-Polish. Altogether, from his whole appearance, with the side-whiskers à la Franz Joseph, it was impossible to tell that he was of Jewish descent.
Walking along like this with Bialik, I say to him: "Did you notice the elderly gentleman who greeted me? Do you know that he is of Jewish descent and is still a Jew? Just imagine — to make such a Jew into a Zionist!" I thought he would leave me in peace. I convinced him what types of Jews the Sosnowiec assimilationists are, but Bialik did not give up his idea, and he pressed me [lit. "took me on the tsitbl"[?]] to tell him about every detail of this assimilationist type; and when he heard from me that he was an intelligent, well-read man, versed in Polish, German and Russian literature, Bialik says to me: "I will make an effort to make this person a Zionist."
In Sosnowiec at that time there was a small café-patisserie (cukiernia) called the "Warsaw Cukiernia"; older officials of the customs office, of the railway, etc. used to gather there. Kampiński had his old friends there, who used to gather every day after lunch at a small table in the "Warsaw Cukiernia" and spend several hours there — and that is indeed where I found the suitable place for bringing Bialik together with Kampiński. Our comrade Weinberg was also one of Kampiński's "good brothers" who used to spend time together in the Warsaw Cukiernia, and he helped me to interest Kampiński in getting to know Bialik.
For this purpose we sat down at a separate table, and a very interesting conversation began between Bialik and Kampiński.
At first they spoke about literature, about poetry in general; gradually, step by step, Bialik moved over to the subject of the great injustice being committed against an ancient historic people, which has given the world such great men. Such a great literature — and it should be so enslaved in exile, and no one takes up the great injustice, to improve the situation of this people.
