A brochure by the Częstochowa rabbi on shechita.
In connection with the attack on Jewish ritual slaughter, the Częstochowa kehilla has published a brochure in Polish by the local rabbi, Rabbi Nachum Asz, entitled "In Defence of Shechita".
In this interesting brochure the author treats Jewish ritual slaughter, in separate chapters, from the religious, legal and scientific standpoints, drawing on a rich number of quotations from the Talmud and from Talmudic literature.
As a motto to the brochure, the following words of the great Polish poet Mickiewicz are quoted:
"The laws of Moses, the most humane of all laws that were binding in antiquity, commanded care for animals, ordered [?] and fixed a time of rest even for the earth; in this provision of the Law of Moses there lies far more philosophical depth than in all the formulas of German philosophy."
In conclusion the author turns to the ruling circles, asking that they preserve the old Polish principles of tolerance towards the Jewish faith.
Heard and Seen

By Ben Amoz.

New times — old songs...
Time makes giant progress, technology works[?] wonders, scientific discoveries are made, the map of the world is changed, but when one looks around at what is going on around us, it seems that we are living now in the epoch of thousands of years ago, because as regards us the general situation has not changed at all; only the "ralisn"[?] (probably: the stage wings) have changed, but the content of the "Jewish play" is the same as once, when one king ruled over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces, when such little kingdoms as in the twentieth century did not yet exist.
There is only one difference. Once Haman demanded "to kill and to destroy all the Jews", to slaughter and annihilate all Jews, and today these slogans are preached by cultured people, by academics, by hot-blooded patriots. Once the antisemites invented that "the Jews do not want to bear the burden of the state, do not want to pay the state taxes", and today, in the civilised century, a woman, a great animal-protection activist, has discovered that we Jews are cruel, barbarians, and have no pity even on the dumb beasts... (an allusion to the bill against ritual slaughter.)
In our own little world too nothing has changed, no change whatsoever has come about; only the persons playing the leading roles have changed. But the song is the same and the streets are the same; the only difference consists in this, that in the year 1929 the song was sung by the gentlemen of the Agudah camp, and in the year 1936 — by hundred-percent Zionists on whose banner is inscribed:
— Kingdom of Israel!..
Here lies before us an appeal of the Będzin Revisionist org[anisation] to the Jews of Będzin not to give a single grosz to the "Keren Hayesod", which is a holy "great and terrible lie"... not to support the fund, for whose money "the sufferings[?] are desecrated, for which generations perished for the sanctification of the Name", and:
Fight the "Keren Hayesod"
Down with the lie
Down with the bluff.
We do not wish to enter into a discussion and point out the senselessness of the counter-action; that is not our task, and above all this is no news for the Będzin "Keren Hayesod" payers, since the "Agudah" in the year 1929, when the poet Leib Yaffe came for the first time to proclaim the "Keren Hayesod" campaign in Będzin, sang the same little song that the "kingdom" Zionists sing today...
Therefore we say that the general changes on the world's road have no influence whatsoever on our life in exile; the same blows that the savage man dealt thousands of years ago — we receive today from civilised, cultured people in white gloves, and with the same pamphlets of the "Agudah" Zionists permit themselves — "and[?] both banks of the Jordan", of "Malkhut Shaddai" (the Kingdom of Heaven) and "Malkhut Yisrael" (the Kingdom of Israel).
— New times, old songs...

One does him the favour...
Jews are, after all, known as a stiff-necked people; that title we received already from Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, but such stubborn people as the Jews of Sosnowiec you will not find in any community, not only in Poland but even abroad not.
Here, for example. If another community had the privilege of having such a witty kehilla commissioner — one who did not have such merits in the field of kehilla affairs — if he had done just one eighth of an eighth of what the Sosnowiec one has managed to do, for example, if he had only thrown the gmilus-khesed (free-loan) fund out of the kehilla premises, or not permitted a Mizrachi rabbi to speak in the synagogue about the "Keren Hayesod", or I-don't-know-what — the kehilla people would surely carry such a head of the community on their hands and kiss the ground on which he trod...
And what are we in Sosnowiec? — Backwardness, indifference; apart from the kehilla officials, nobody shows any sign of gratitude; not to speak of the national camp, which is known as a disloyal element, but also the religious section, for whom the kehilla commissioner takes such care that their needs should not be disturbed — is ungrateful and does not pay the proper respect to the great man, to the "redeemer of the city"...
For example, the board of the "Talmud Torah" in Sosnowiec proclaimed a pledge (nedarim) campaign; the board, with the chairman at its head, should surely have come to the kehilla commissioner and said:
— "My lord, we, your humble servants, come to you to ask permission to proclaim the pledge campaign for the benefit of the Talmud Torah and to permit speaking in the synagogue about the campaign."
But the board did not do so; instead, exactly like the disloyal ones — "free in the 'free school'"[?], and the chairman R' Leibish Szwajcer (woe to that shame..) took it upon himself, without permission from Mr Commissioner, to speak to the worshippers before the Torah reading, that they should pledge for the benefit of the Talmud Torah. Has such a thing ever been heard? Has such an "outrage" been heard of?...
What did the commissioner do? What did Mr Commissioner do? He did not, God forbid, punish the refractory chairman of the Talmud Torah, but behaved like the simple-hearted honest Jews of old: he went off to "the Kingdom" (the authorities) and complained:
— "The Jews have rebelled against me again"...
— Who is the new rebel? — the Kingdom asked.
— The chairman of the "Miejscowa Talmud-Tora" (the local Talmud Torah)...
— Calm yourself, my dear — the Kingdom said — I will send for him and tell him a few words of reproof. — Calm yourself.
The Kingdom kept its word, sent for the chairman and asked him:
— Why did you not obtain from Mr Commissioner permission to speak in the synagogue?
— "Proszę pana" (please, sir), what great sin have I committed? If I want to speak in the synagogue in order to help[?] support the institution where 400 poor Jewish children study, must I first ask permission for it? Let Mr Commissioner pay out the subsidy, as the former dozór (kehilla boards) did, and then perhaps we will give up the penny pledge campaign. So why is he so angry?
— "Bardzo słusznie" (quite right) — the Kingdom answered — but what harm can it do you to ask him permission to speak in the synagogue, if he wants "that"?
— One does him the favour...
Dr. Rotenstreich receives a delegation of Zagłębie Jews in Eretz Israel — 35 families from Zagłębie to settle on the land

As your correspondent has already reported, the first founding meeting of olim from Zagłębie and Silesia resolved to settle a certain number of families from Zagłębie on Keren Kayemet land — some of those who already live in Eretz Israel today and some of those who are still abroad — who will become colonists.
In accordance with this resolution the committee of the association took upon itself to carry the resolution out, and turned to the central office in Jerusalem with an inquiry on the matter.
A few days later the association received a reply from the representative of the Jewish Agency, Dr. Pras.[?] F. Rotenstreich, who asked that a delegation come to Jerusalem to discuss the matter.
The delegation consisted of Messrs. chairman[?] Binyamin Dgiali (Fiszel), Dr. G. Bruin (former director of the „Yavneh“ gymnasium in Będzin, now a lecturer at the Hebrew University in Jerusalem), Shmuel Abramowicz (G.[?] commissioner of the KKL in Sosnowiec) and Fiszel Bacza (Sosnowiec).
The delegation demanded that the Agency fulfil its „promise“ given in 1925 in favour of the Jews of Zagłębie. To this Dr. Rotenstreich solemnly declared that he is ready to support the project by every means. He also immediately came to an understanding with the head of the settlement department, Dr. Hexter, and the latter asked that within the next few days a list of the first group wishing to settle be submitted to him.
For this purpose a general meeting of olim from Zagłębie and Silesia was held under the chairmanship of Mr. Fiszel, before which Dr. Zgorodzki[?] presented the plan for the colony. The meeting was very lively. The participants showed broad interest in the colonisation project. After a lengthy discussion 35 families signed up, from: Sosnowiec (14), Będzin (6), Dąbrowa (1), Charoszów[?] (3), Zawiercie (5), Olkusz (2), Myszków (2) and Czeladź (2).
Two banks have already come forward, with which negotiations are being conducted on loans for the families that need capital for settling in.
The meeting, which lasted until late at night, closed with the singing of „Hatikvah“.
Families interested in the question of colonisation are asked to apply to the above-mentioned association through the „Zaglembier Tsaytung“.
The struggle against „Amalek“ still goes on (an old little tale from the Chumash that one must remember well)

Already in very ancient times Amalek — a nation of beasts and ugly, dull-witted obstinate men — set itself the goal of fighting the Children of Israel. And so it fell upon them right after their redemption from Egypt, at Rephidim, on the way to the Promised Land, and began its fight first with the stragglers, the weaker ones, who are more easily bent and beaten.
But the Jewish leader, Moses, sensed what was brewing and without delay ordered the mobilisation of the best forces of the people, who well understand the meaning of honour and freedom of a nation, especially in its first steps towards independence, to go out into an open fight of life and death with Amalek. He himself, the leader, took up a higher position to direct the battle and observe how the Children of Israel were defending their honour.
The mobilised best forces properly appreciated the essence of such a[?] battle with Amalek, obeyed the leadership and fought stubbornly and successfully.
But probably the political situation, given the circumstances of the time, was not always favourable to the leadership, for which reason it was forced [—] to let its hands drop... and a misfortune: as soon as the Children of Israel noticed that the leadership was no longer directing with the same zeal as before, they too grew weak in the fight, and it turned out that victory was already passing to Amalek's side...
And the leader's friends saw that his hands were already dropping. The difficulties on all sides grow ever greater, and there is a danger that the whole struggle so far may, God forbid, go to waste — and before the people still stands such a strong wall: the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Jebusite and Girgashite, who are already clenching[?] their fists too... what will become of it then? So they did everything possible to hold up the leader's hands from both sides, and they succeeded in convincing the masses that although stones are being laid and the hands are heavy, they are faithful and still hold firm as at the beginning of the fight, and when nothing else is possible, the leadership must stand in the position of an onlooker from the side.
And this time the victory was complete on the side of the Children of Israel...
And history indeed did not keep them waiting long, and the Children of Israel already stand once again in a great war with the same Amalek; and lo, the first Jewish king, under pressure from some people who had taken a liking to the fat sheep and the fine Amalekite produce, allowed himself to weaken the holy national struggle a little — for which he came off very badly and had to yield his place to one better than he, who did know what the honour of a nation means...
An old little tale from the Chumash, which one must nevertheless remember well, because „Amalek“ is already sticking in our[?] throat far too much.
Oy, what an Amalek!!!
Y. B.
A Little Feuilleton. — A Letter from an Aryan Bull to the League of Nations

[Satirical feuilleton — Germany, Nuremberg Laws.] A letter from an Aryan bull to the League of Nations.
In many regions of Germany the Nuremberg Laws are being applied a l s o to... cattle...
(From the newspapers)
"Highly esteemed human institution for human rights and for peace:
Allow me, as the representative of the cattle in Germany, both the Aryan and the non-Aryan, to submit to you the following memorandum ["memoriom"], which we ask you only to read with great attention and to take measures to satisfy our demand and request.
As you probably know (we cattle think that the League of Nations ought to know about such things), the Nuremberg Laws have been introduced among us, upon our society, upon the cattle. Well, as far as people are concerned, we neither want to nor can take care of their affairs; after all, they are not cattle, so they can look after themselves. But regarding us cattle, an unheard-of injustice has been committed.
Ever since cattle have existed in the world, it has never happened that there should be distinctions[?] of class and racial character among us.
Among us there has never been any difference between the red heifer and the ox that is tam [harmless]; even the calf, our forefather, was no aristocrat of lineage either. We all go dressed in our own, one and the same hide-clothes, we all wear horns, some bigger and some smaller. We all eat grass — not one getting better and another worse. So it has been among us cattle since the world has stood.
And suddenly they have come and want to introduce among us, too, the "fine" customs that exist among people — at any rate, among the present-day Germans.
What right does a human being have to meddle in our intimate affairs? Whose business is it, I ask, if a bull from Germany wants to fall in love with a cow that belongs to a Jew? Especially since a beast can belong to a Jew today and tomorrow — to a non-Jew...
We, the cattle of Germany, express the sharpest protest against the Nuremberg Laws in general and against the restrictions on cattle in particular. And we hereby warn the Germans that if they nevertheless carry out their wild laws concerning us, we shall take our own measures: we shall butt with our horns, we shall trample their bellies, which are empty today, we shall split their foolish heads, in which there is nothing but wild Nazism and cruel stupidity.
In order to avoid such conflicts between us and the Germans, we ask the League of Nations to take in good time the proper measures against the crazy Germans.
If you, members of the League of Nations, are not able to do anything for people, you must do something for the cattle, and if not — we shall be compelled to found a cattle League of Nations"...
Rebus.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Terumah)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion, charity.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Terumah
a) "That they take for Me an offering" (Ex. 25:2)
"For Me — for My name's sake." Rashi.
This is a fine point: only for the Tabernacle did the giving of charity have to be for its own sake; but with other charities the act of giving itself matters more than the intention.. Kohelet Yitzhak.
* * *
"When Israel said 'we will do and we will hear', at once the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: 'that they take for Me an offering'." Yalkut Reuveni.
"We will do and we will hear" — before one starts to reflect: that is what is needed in charity. Give when the feeling comes, before one starts to reflect whether one can give, whether giving to so-and-so is really a mitzvah, and the like... Imrei Noam.
* * *
The pious Rothschild, Reb Shimon Netanel, was once walking through the streets of Frankfurt. A poor man comes up to him and pours out his heart: he has a grown-up daughter whom he has no means to marry off; he asks him for help and asks when he may come to him.
Reb Shimon Netanel searches his pocket and finds no money — so he pulls off his gold watch and hands it to the poor Jew: go and sell this.
The Jew is startled and astonished: would it not have been better had he told him to come for money tomorrow?
Reb Shimon Netanel answers him:
— At that moment a great pity seized me; had I told you to come to me tomorrow, perhaps by then the pity would already have cooled in me — therefore I pulled the watch off myself in the heat of the minute...
* * *
The Chatam Sofer once came to ask a stingy Pressburg magnate for a donation. At first the magnate refused to give anything. Only after long persuasion did he manage to get a small donation out of him.
As he was leaving, the Chatam Sofer says to him:
— Thank God...
The magnate says:
— I give to you, and you thank God!
The Chatam Sofer answers him:
— In truth the money is not yours: "The silver is Mine and the gold is Mine, saith the Lord"; only, in Berakhot folio 35 the Gemara says that after the blessing — after a person does God's will with a thing — he acquires the thing. Well, you did not want to do any charity with this money, so the money is not yours but God's, and what I took, I really took from God; so I must thank God and not you...
* * *
To Kraków there once came the well-known emissary (shadar) from Safed, Reb Naftali Chanoles[?], to collect money for the Land of Israel. He went to ask a donation of the famous magnate Reb Yoel Bzhiminger[?]. Reb Naftali Chanoles was a sharp man, and when Reb Yoel did not want to give him the requested sum quickly enough, he simply shouted at him.
Reb Yoel says to him:
— You don't know how to collect money; you talk too sharply. When one comes to a magnate for a donation one must speak gently, not as harshly as you.
— If so — says Reb Naftali — if you understand[?] better how to talk to magnates and ask them for donations, then it is more fitting that I should sit at home and you should become a shadar and collect donations..
* * *
In Słonim there was a rich miser who did not want to give a penny to charity; on the other hand, for honorific[?] mitzvot he really pushed himself forward — to stand at the reader's desk and lead the prayers before the amud ad"g[?].
Reb Eizel[?] says of him:
— He is a "holy of holies", for in Chullin folio 7 the Gemara says: "Israel are holy. There is one who has and does not want [to give], and there is one who wants and has not." In charity our magnate is a "has and does not want" (he has the means, only he doesn't want) — so he is a holy man; at the reader's desk he is a "wants and has not" (he wants, only he can't) — so he is a holy man once again; so he is a holy of holies...
* * *
A rich man once told the Sanzer Rav how much charity he gives, adding, as is the custom, "no evil eye" [literally "may it not be spoken out"].
The Sanzer Rav says to him:
— Give, and speak it out... [pun: "say it all out"]
* * *
Reb Avishl Frankfurter used to distribute whatever he possessed. One of his intimates argued with him: "He who spends [on charity] should not spend more than a fifth" — more than a fifth of what one possesses one need not give away.
Reb Avishl answers:
— That is indeed the law; but of charity it is said "the more charity, the more life" — so it is a matter of saving life, and saving life overrides even the Sabbath, and all the more so a rabbinic commandment. Imrei Tzaddikim[?].
* * *
The Sanzer Rav too was a great lavish giver in matters of charity, and when he was reminded of the above-mentioned Gemara, he answered:
— "And redeem thy sins by charity" — with charity one redeems one's sins. Well, the Gemara speaks of ordinary people; but I am such a great sinner that I must give much charity to redeem my sins...
A World Turned Upside Down...

[Humour and satire — "The Cooking Ladle": a poem.]
A world turned upside down — now there is
no more summer or winter,
justice has vanished, truth has died,
the world and man change[?] everywhere[?].
Sabbath is no Sabbath: now it snows
and now it rains,
now it freezes and soon it is mud,
now a man harnesses his little horse
to the sleigh —
and soon he regrets it again...
Nothing is firm now, everything
wobbles and spins;
so it is in the land of Abyssinia:
now the Blacks attack[?]
with valour,
and tomorrow it is Mussolini again....
How long did the sanction fight with
energy
against the fist and the aggressors —
and what name do those same
fighters now have
with every Jew?
Who comes out against shechita (ritual slaughter)
in the city council, in the Sejm or in the gmina?
Who, if not those who hold the say
and now run the state?
Something — a [—][?] — awaits, tremendous,
uncanny:
experts and devil-machines,
so that tomorrow a Jew in the whole country
will not find a quiet corner.
Hershele.

Khatskele Kalbonik on the Public Fast

[Humour and satire — "The Cooking Ladle": shechita and the public fast; a dialect monologue.]
"The Cooking Ladle" — humour and satire, compiled by Amotzlo.

Fellows[?]!
Last Friday[?] I told you the story of the shechita: that Maciek[?] wants to slaughter glatt kosher and Jasiek[?] is to be the mashgiach. Well, there was an alarm, all the deputies went [—] to the minister himself.
Now I'll tell you a new story: the rabbinate got going, held a whole conference and ruled that there must be a [—][?] fast exactly like Yom Kippur.
Well, what do you say to that, fellows? I say the rabbinate is right: there really must be a fast, and let the antisemites[?] see that Jews too have a strength — to fast. But if they ask me whether our fellows must also fast, I'll say this:
— Listen[?] to me: I say the rabbinate is right, there really must be a fast, but it's the fat schmaltz-bellies[?] who need to fast. They'll ask me: why not also the Podzamcze folk? I'll answer you: because, now, the Podzamcze fellows fast all year round. Got it? That's how I'll answer when they ask me.
I'd tell you something more, but I've talked so much about fasting that I've started to get hungry, and when I'm hungry I can't utter a word. So have a good Shabbes and stay healthy.
Public Declaration!

[Humour and satire — "The Cooking Ladle": a parody of a Sosnowiec kehilla bigwig.]
Although no one asks me and no one demands anything of me, I nevertheless make the following declaration. For I am, after all, not some plain flesh-and-blood mortal — I am preserved and marinated in royal spices, every important person[?] bows to me threefold; is that a trifle?!
Quickly to the point: in the name of the "Schiller"[?], I first recite a "prayer of announcement" (pun on "prayer of thanksgiving")... and declare:
1) I took no part in the festivity of "świniobicie" (pig-slaughtering) in Ostrów[?].
2) This month I blessed the new moon.
3) I took no part in the consultation at the Small Traders' Association because, quite simply, none of the initiators had the slightest thought of inviting me...
Ah, you will surely ask: if they did not invite me, why do I issue such "clever" declarations? A hard question indeed, but what am I, poor thing, to do? Since I received the "szlify" (insignia of rank), I suffer from a mania for giving sermons and writing nonsense...

What Grooms and Brides Must Know

[Humour and satire — "The Cooking Ladle": advice for the betrothed.]
Advice for young men who are about to get married.
1. Take a flat with as few doors as possible — you will have a couple fewer doors to slam during a quarrel.
2. Do not buy heavy vases and flowerpots — they may one day come down on your heads.
3. Do not buy luxury furniture — you will have to dry nappies on it all the same.
4. Let your bedroom be large and roomy, so that the curses your wife will give you have room to spread out.
5. Buy a big dining table, so that you are kept apart from one another — that is a charm for domestic peace.
6. Do not buy crystal ware — when one gets angry one cannot tell crystal from ordinary glass.
7. Provide yourself with several clocks, so that when you come home late you can prove to your wife that none of the clocks is right.

The “Specialists” of the “Ubezpieczalnia”.

A doctor from the “Ubezpieczalnia” (the social health-insurance fund) was called out to a sick man. After the examination the doctor says to the patient's wife:

— If so, you are still lucky; if he were not a dyer, things would be very bitter.
Charity.

The famous English humorist Bernard Shaw noticed at a charity ball in London an older, plain girl with whom nobody had danced. So he went up to her and invited her to a dance. The girl felt very happy and in the middle of the dance she said:
— I thank you for the great pleasure...
— Who is talking of pleasure — Shaw interrupted her — you have forgotten, miss, that this is a charity ball, and here one does everything only for charity's sake...

A gripping tragic novel about an ilui (prodigy)
(76
Because of that, however, Nachum had to leave the place at once. For a whole day he ran about the streets of New York like a madman, and when he felt that his strength was giving out, he decided, after such a long time of disappearance [?], to turn again to Benigl for help.
But how broken he was when he heard from fat Beyle that Benigl had gone away and would come back only in two weeks' time.
Her words struck his sick brain as with a heavy hammer, and suddenly...
Limping Chinese men in long coats began to dance before him; before his eyes flew thousands of red "turpelekh" [?] filled with hot powder, and in the middle, among them, stands Balbina, alive [?], with great nails like a cat's, with bared teeth, dancing with the Chinese...
He feels a strong blow, it seems, from his own body. He sees a Chinese man together with Balbina seize him, choke [?] him and pour hot water over him. He tears himself away from them, runs up to Balbina, throws himself on her and wants to strangle her. But she is stronger than he, pushes him back and he falls. He falls into a deep black abyss, where it is so dark, and yet through the dense darkness he sees Balbina's figure cut itself out, coming towards him with outstretched hands that also have long nails...
He opens his eyes, looks around and sees before him a white, bright room. Where is he? — he asks himself.
And at that same moment, from the head of the bed, a woman's head bent over his head, the head of a beautiful young woman.
— It seems to be her, Balbina. Yes, Balbina! How does she come to be here? What is she doing here?
As if in a convulsion he shuddered and, shutting his eyes, began to scream:
— Balbina! Away from me, what do you want? You snake! Snake, let me go!
— God in heaven! Can this be possible?... — the woman, who was none other than Rachele, began to cry out, and ran closer to Nachum, who lay with closed eyes.
— Who are you? — she fell upon him and began to speak to him — I am not Balbina, look well, see, I am..
— It's all the same to me, give me cocaine, give me "India" [?] — he began to scream and to tear the shirt off his body.
— Doctor, quickly, faster — Rachele calls the doctor of the old-age home.
And it did not take long before a black carriage carried away a man bound in a straitjacket, and beside him sat Rachele and the doctor. Thus Nachum was taken to one of the psychiatric hospitals for narcotics addicts.
— How is the Jew from the twelfth room? — Moshele asked Rachele when she came back.
— You know, "mames" [?], that Jew had to be transferred to a hospital for the mentally ill; that is what the doctor ordered.
— Pity on him — said Moshele, sadly shaking his head.
But Rachele no longer heard the words. She could not stand still in one place and, running about the room with stifled weeping, she cried out:
— God, can this be... "prz" [?] my mother's... father...
Chapter 26.
And once again days of suffering and pain began for Balbina.
It is not destined for her, it seems, to have a quiet, comfortable and contented life.
At every step she feels how the curse of her husband's little boy, of little Moshele, who spat on her and cursed her, pursues her.
His words, which the boy said to her then, will always ring in her ears. Never will she forget his eyes, from which a fire of contempt and hatred [?] sprayed then at her, at Balbina, who had taken his father from him.
And despite the fact that this is already in the distant past, despite the fact that several years already separate her from the day when she saw the boy in her home, his words still ring in her ears, stabbing her as with spears, as with pointed sharp knives.
— Always and forever will I weep — she hears the boy's words — forever will I weep and my tears will fall at your feet.
She is already tired; she understands that it is her duty to run to Leon, who is in Hollywood. She feels that her heart still longs for him even now. But how can she cast off Max, who has surrounded her with such ardent love? How can she now come to him and reveal her secret, that she does not love him but Leon, for whom she longs? He will surely not bear it, he will surely lose his mind.

The Kehilla Council Will Have to Start Again from "Bereshit"...

[Będzin — kehilla.]
The board sends the kehilla budget back to the council.
On Tuesday the kehilla board held a meeting. On the agenda: setting the new budget, a report on the past year's activity, and engaging a cantor for the beit midrash.
On the first item, board member (dozór) Mr. Skocylas (Agudah) proposed that, since the council meetings on the budget had taken place without a quorum, the budget should be sent back to the council to be considered once more.
Board member Hampel spoke against the proposal, saying that, first, it is not within the board's competence to check whether the council's budget meetings take place at the proper dates, and above all the council meetings had taken place at the second date, when they are valid with any number of members present.
Mr. Hampel's opinion was supported by board member Manele. But the chairman puts the Agudah proposal to a vote, and by 5 votes to 3 the proposal is adopted.
The second item was postponed. As to engaging a cantor for the beit midrash, it was decided that the main candidates, Goyim [?] and Berman, should lead the prayers on trial in the presence of the board.
Mass Meeting against the Legislative Council.

[Będzin — Zionism and politics.]
On Sunday the N.Z.O. [?] (New Zionist Organization) in Będzin organized a mass meeting about the Legislative Council [in Palestine].
Besides the "Agudah", economic organizations such as the merchants' union, the small traders' union and the artisans' union also joined the protest.
The meeting was organized in perfect "ritual purity": out of tolerance toward the "Agudah" the gallery was reserved for women, and even Mr. Klozman did not dare to speak bareheaded...
The picture of the presidium itself was a fulfilment of the prophecy "the wolf shall dwell with the lamb"...
The chairman was the Revisionist activist Mr. Abraham Diament, and the assessors were Messrs. Józef Tuchsznajder (artisans), Herszel Dimant [?], Dawid [?] Skocylas, Szlomo Icchak Rinski (Agudah), Abraham Meir Herzberg (secretary of the rabbinate), D. Wilbergaler [?], Mendel Rapszik, Efraim Klajman, councillor Grosman (artisans) and the parnas Kisner (Revisionist).
The first speech was given by the chairman. He spoke about the ritual-slaughter decree, antisemitism, the Zionist Executive, and related that the Zionists Landauer and Wygodzki [?] had gone from house to house agitating against the campaign of "Mrs. [?] Cohen". At the same time he smiled at the representatives of the "Agudah" and declared that the "Agudah" people stand higher in his eyes than all the Zionist great men with their rabbis, even with their doctors...
The parnas Rinski speaks with enthusiasm about the heroic deeds of the halutzim in Eretz Israel and comes out against the Legislative Council project, but he consoles the listeners that the decree will be annulled.
The secretary of the rabbinate, comrade Herzberg, comes out with sharp complaints against the English government; his greatest complaint, however, is against the Zionist "heroes" [?], "who conduct a ma-yafit [obsequious] policy"...
Mr. Klajman says that in the present time the artisans too must have their say in political affairs. In passing he relates that a female relative of his writes to him that the Arab organizations "stage" and incite not to sell land to the Jews.
Then the floor is given to the general secretary of Brit ha-Tzohar, Mr. J. Klarman, who came from Warsaw on account of the "match" with the "Agudah". Mr. K. speaks about the wave of antisemitism in the whole world and about the decree of the Legislative Council, but he promises that "as long as" there are Betarim in Eretz Israel and the spirit of Jabotinsky hovers there, the Legislative Council will not be allowed.
After several resolutions against the Legislative Council and the ritual-slaughter decree are adopted, "Hatikvah" is sung. The freshly baked Agudist "Zionists" leave the hall in haste...

Hundreds of Jews Who Came to Say Psalms Found the Synagogue Locked...

[Sosnowiec — religion and community.] As is known, in accordance with the resolution of the Agudat HaRabbanim (rabbis' association), Psalms were recited in public last Thursday in all synagogues, batei midrash and prayer houses throughout Poland.
In our town, too, the resolution was carried out, and in all the batei midrash and shtiblekh Jews said Psalms and prayed that the shechita decree [the ban on ritual slaughter] be annulled.
But how great was the anger and bitterness of the local Jews when, coming to say Psalms in the (main) synagogue, they found the synagogue locked.
As we are informed, the synagogue was locked so that the crowd should not dirty the floor of the synagogue, which had been washed in honour of the Sabbath guests...
— Comment is superfluous.
An Unsuccessful "Operation".

[Sosnowiec — fraud.] The local resident D. Blipre[?] got the urge to grab an easy little profit. To this end he took out 2 savings books of the K.K.O. [municipal savings bank] in Katowice. Into one book he deposited 1 zł and into the second 2 zł. Then he made the figure 1 into 800 and the figure 2 into 1300.
With the books he came to Będzin, where he bought textile (manufaktura) goods from the firm of H. Unger, and besides his own bills of exchange he gave the K.K.O. books as a deposit.
A few days later, however, the "operation" was discovered in the following circumstances: when the employee of the above-mentioned firm came to the K.K.O. to inquire about the genuineness of the books, he was at once detained; only when Blipre was arrested was the employee released.

An Interesting Budget Debate at the Plenum of the Kehilla Council

[Page heading: “Life in Kielce” (Dos lebn in Kielts) — Friday, 5 Adar 5696 — piątek 28 lutego 1936 (Friday, 28 February 1936).]
Under the chairmanship of President A. Piotrkowski, the plenary sessions of the Kielce kehilla council on the budget for the year 1936 began on Sunday.
The sessions lasted 2 days, Sunday and Tuesday.
Before proceeding to the budget debate, parnas Fiszman read out a letter from the Central Union of Small Traders in Poland to the Kielce branch about convening an urgent conference of all kehillot, merchants' and small traders' associations of the Kielce voivodeship concerning the terrible boycott campaign being conducted by Endek gangs in many towns and townlets of the Kielce voivodeship.
On parnas Fiszman's proposal a discussion was opened, in which Messrs. Gutman, Lejchter, Director Rozenberg, M. D. Ejzenberg and President Goldman took part. Some speakers declared themselves in favour of a conference of the kehillot without the participation of the economic organisations, and some were against a conference — and this because of the old bankrupt [illegible word — “principle”/“tune”?] of... “Happy is the man who is always afraid”..., because of the “contact” with the government, and the like.
Secretary Sokołowski informed the council about the exchange of letters between the parliamentary Sejm “Koło” [the Jewish Club in the Sejm] and the kehilla regarding the planned conference, and read out the letter of Deputy Sommerstein on this important matter.
Finally it was resolved to convene the kehillot conference after all, and the technical work for the conference, as well as drafting the agenda, was handed over to the board.
After the long “political” discussion the budget debate began.
Then parnas Fiszman again took the floor and sharply attacked the presidiums of the council and of the board, which rarely convene sessions of the council and of the board. He demanded that sessions of the council be convened more often and that an audit committee be elected to supervise the kehilla's finances.
Board member (dozór) Gutman spoke at greater length. He pointed to the demoralisation and lawlessness (hefkerut) that have lately prevailed in public life. Public work is nowadays run by people with whom it is even dangerous to sit at the same table, for fear that the content of the conversations will be carried out into the street and passed on elsewhere... As proof of this social decline Mr. Gutman pointed to the fatal result of the last elections to the Kielce city council, in which there are no more than 2 (two) Jews; to the unheard-of manner in which the election campaign itself was conducted; and to the “famous” negotiations with the decisive circles on the part of well-known Jewish “communal activists”, who bear — and will long bear — on their conscience the moral blow and the insult suffered by the Jewish community of 20 thousand in Kielce during the city council elections.
The vice-president of the council, Mr. M. Sz. Fryd, complained: why is the kehilla tax (the “etat”) not being collected, why was no coal campaign carried out this winter, and why is so little money distributed every year for kimcha de-Pischa (Passover flour relief)?
Board members (dozors) Lejchter and Winiasz[?] very sharply criticise the members of the council for not taking an interest in kehilla work, which rests exclusively on the shoulders of the kehilla president, Mr. Goldman, who is literally collapsing under the heavy burden of the day-to-day thankless work in the kehilla, without any help from the board members and parnasim, even neglecting his private business.
In the same vein spoke also board member M. D. Ejzenberg, parnas J. Kan and others.
President Goldman, in a longer speech, answered all the opponents, pointing to his cooperation with all members of the council and the board for the good of the kehilla. He also pointed to the devoted work of President Piotrkowski, thanks to whom various social and philanthropic campaigns of the kehilla are carried out successfully.
“We,” Mr. Goldman concluded his speech, “have sufficient good will for the kehilla work; only help us and do not trip us up, as some parnasim do and want to do — and then our work will be fruitful in all respects.”
After the budget revenues had been adopted, the discussion on the budget expenditures began.
We shall give the further report in the next issue.
Festive Opening of the Eretz-Israel Bazaar

Tonight, Saturday night, at 9 p.m., the festive opening of the Eretz-Israel bazaar will take place at the Zionist club.
The bazaar will last 5 days, i.e. until Wednesday, 4 March inclusive.
The programme of the bazaar is as follows:
Saturday, 9 p.m. — the festive opening; half past nine — a major lecture by Adv. Hartglas. After the lecture the guests will view the bazaar, and various entertainments will take place.
Sunday, 1 March, 5 p.m. — a performance for the school youth; 9 p.m. — a dancing — “A Night in the Orchard (Pardes)”.
Monday, 2 March, 5 p.m. — a performance for the school youth; 9 p.m. — a vocal-musical concert; after the concert — dancing.
Tuesday, 3 March, half past 8 p.m. — a recitation evening by Żak Lewi (Warsaw).
Wednesday, 4 March, 9 p.m. — a farewell ball, a “living newspaper” and the festive closing of the bazaar.
The bazaar will be most imposing and will without doubt delight the eye of all visitors.

Dr. Gaszewski murdered in Warsaw.

The murderer is a worker dismissed in a staff reduction.
On Wednesday in the daytime, on Czerniakowska Street in Warsaw, the deputy director of the "ZUPU" [the Insurance Institution for White-Collar Workers], formerly director of the "Ubezpieczalnia" [Social Insurance Office] in Sosnowiec, Dr. Gaszewski [?], was murdered.
The attack was carried out as he was about to get into a car that was waiting for him. At that same moment a person ran up and opened fire, from which Gaszewski fell dead on the spot.
When the murderer was detained he said: "He took away my bread, so I took away his life."
The murderer is a Sosnowiec man. His name is Aleksy Szymik [?], he lives at 1 Maja [Street] number 3. A former clerk of the "ZUPU" institution in Sosnowiec. Half a year ago he was made redundant by Gaszewski, who was the director at the time.
—o—
Merchants' Association in new premises.
The Merchants' and Industrialists' Association in Sosnowiec has been moved to new premises on 3 Maja Street.
—o—
Endek troublemakers wanted to provoke anti-Jewish disturbances in Pilica.
But they came to an ugly end.
On Tuesday, market day, two young Endeks came to Pilica with the aim of provoking anti-Jewish disturbances. To this end the fellows posted themselves in the middle of the market in order to provoke a brawl. As it happened, a Jew who was running[?] bumped into one of the gang. At once they threw themselves on the Jew and beat him badly. When the local Christian householders, among them also the wójt [head of the commune], reacted to this as was proper, the hooligans beat them too. And so a brawl broke out in the market. Police arrived on the spot, detained the "heroes" and later transported them to Sosnowiec, to the investigation office.
As we are informed[?], one[?] of the "heroes" is a court trainee (aplikant).
Great success of Będzin "Hakoach" in Bielsko.

The "Maccabi" in Bielsko (Bielitz) celebrated its 40th jubilee, to which the Będzin "Hakoach" was also invited.
Although the present management of "Hakoach" has been active for only a few months, "Hakoach" nevertheless took part in all the competitions with the greatest success and received the largest number of prizes.
The first prize for gymnastics (a gold badge) was taken by Bożykowski, 2nd[?] prize (a silver badge) — Cukierman, 3rd prize — Szenfeld; prizes were also received by the participants in the volleyball (siatkówka) and basketball (koszykówka) displays. Apart from that Mr. Bożykowski, as the best gymnast, received a fine gift.
In connection with this, on Saturday night the 18th of this month a celebration will take place in the premises of "Hakoach", at which the prizes will be distributed.
—o—
On export to Finland.
This week the officer for economic affairs, Mr. S.[?] Gerstedt of Finland, stayed in Zagłębie, with the purpose of acquainting himself with the local trade market in general and of making use of the Finnish trade market for Polish exports.
Terrible storm over Zagłębie.

Trees torn out with their roots. — Sudden death during the storm. — Considerable damage.
On Wednesday towards evening a violent storm passed over Zagłębie, combined with a strong gale and hail.
In many places the storm-wind tore out trees with their roots and ripped off roofs.
In the municipal night shelter[?] ("nakht-hoyz") in Sosnowiec 16 window-panes were smashed by a thunderclap.
At the "Saturn" coal mine in Czeladź the mine foreman (sztygar) Gąsowski[?] suffered a heart attack from fright.
Normal tram communication was interrupted for a certain time.
The storm caused great damage to the grain fields.
In Sławków the 67[?]-year-old Hirszl Ring died suddenly of fright.
In Będzin a thunderbolt entered the apartment of Sz. Frajberg, Czeladzka Street, and went back out through the ceiling.

In connection with the kehilla elections in Sosnowiec a meeting took place with the participation of representatives of all the guilds. On the agenda was the position of the artisans towards the kehilla elections.

The "Expres Zagłębia" Chews Over the Vilest Lies about Jews

[Press — antisemitism.] The "Expres Zagłębia", the favourite organ of our shmendriks, has in recent months been showing its true face with regard to Jews. Every question that has any connection whatsoever with Jews is smeared in that little paper so antisemitically that the "Kurier Zachodni" may already feel ashamed...
In Tuesday's issue the little paper quotes the speech of the president of the Upper Silesian insurgents [powstańcy], Senator Kornke.
The senator sheds crocodile tears over the fact that Katowice is taking on the same appearance as the Będzins and the Sosnowiecs.
"Kaftan-wearers [chałaciarze] at the railway station, at the markets, Jewish restaurants in the streets, kosher slaughter, Hebrew inscriptions on the signboards — this is something every thinking Pole must reflect upon."
Then the little paper chews over the old antisemitic "news" that "the Jews strive to bring harm to Poland in the forum of international politics", that "Jews wriggle out of the most elementary obligations towards the Polish state, for example, they wriggle out of military service, they pay no taxes".
Then come "statistical" figures which "prove" that "the Jews of Katowice and Chorzów pay almost nothing to the fund of "LOPP" [the Air and Anti-Gas Defence League], and so on.
— Have we really already fallen so low that such a little paper should allow itself to spit in the faces of its Jewish readers and advertisers?
What Does the Jewish Combatants' Association in Będzin Declare about the Scandalous Conduct of Its Delegate?

[Będzin — ex-combatants.] From the Jewish combatants in Będzin we have received the following communiqué:
In connection with the notices in the Jewish press concerning the behaviour of our representative at the board meeting of the District Federation in Sosnowiec, we declare the following:
"We state with complete frankness that our delegate committed a great error, but as the only Jewish delegate he was unable to bring it about that the content of the appeal be changed. As regards the signature of our delegate, we declare that this happened not out of ill will, but because he did not grasp the situation. Concerning the person, the Union will draw the appropriate consequences"...
Editor's remark:
The answer resembles the answer of that Jewish woman about the "pot". First — says the woman — I never borrowed any pot; second, the pot was broken; and third, I have, after all, already given the pot back"...
— Our delegate — declares the board of the combatants — did not have the influence to change the content of the well-known appeal; second, he did it without grasping the situation; and third, we shall draw the appropriate consequences from it.
— No, esteemed comrades combatants, your answer does not satisfy the Jewish public at all; it demands the proper satisfaction for the shameful libel cast by your delegate upon the whole Jewish people.
What's New in Upper Silesia? — First Trial for Violating the Foreign-Currency Law

[Upper Silesia — court.] What's new in Upper Silesia?

First trial for violating the foreign-currency law.

In the dock sat Messrs. Rudolf Just and Fritz Danziger, collectors for local and Budapest firms, who were charged with sending 6 letters abroad, each letter containing 20 zł.

Polish coal will be burned in Switzerland.

“In the Tangle of Life”

[Zawiercie — literature / serialised novel.] That is the name of the new novel which begins to be printed in today's issue of the “Zaglembier Tsaytung”.
The novel mirrors a story of two generations. The heroes are a young Hasidic fellow by the name of Dovidl Tajtelbaum of Kraków, whom his parents married off to a Zawiercie girl.

Small Remarks on Great Matters

[Column — Sosnowiec, Będzin, the World Jewish Congress.]
Before the kehilla elections.
All of Jewry in Sosnowiec is under the impression of the new kehilla elections. With this question people get up, and with it they lie down to sleep. Everything and everyone is taken up with this very problem, which in truth plays one of the most important roles in everyday life, in so far as it has any connection with Jewry.
And it is no wonder: the commissarial autocracy stirred up so much bad blood that one man would gladly drown the other in a spoonful of water. All this has concentrated into one mass, which would perhaps gladly take revenge.
And therefore, when we look on and see how the Jewish town councillors have taken the initiative to create a unified list, that is, a common front, this can truly gladden us, and we welcome the useful development, which is capable of bringing much good and enormous benefit into our communal life.
But — we tremble before the "but" — we would dearly wish that no obstacles arise which might, God forbid, disturb the fine idyll of unity, of which we are so greatly in need at all times and on every occasion, let alone nowadays, when every individual seeks to exploit us and to debase our honour, to defile our decency and honesty.
True, at the time of writing these lines the question is on a good path; yet we would wish with all our heart that things not be allowed to come to misunderstandings, which can lead to strife — and then everything is ruined. Mr. X or Mr. Y comes along with his over-clever inventions [?], which are aimed at overturning the building, and he digs and digs, bores and bores, until the hole appears, and then everything is spilled out. No matter — there are such people, who cannot walk the straight road. Such people, who cannot live while the sun is shining, but only in darkness and on crooked and twisted paths; there they feel like the worm in horseradish, like the bat in the dark.
That is of whom and why we are afraid. In general, we have always known that the Sosnowiec Jew, the communal activist and the "stirring-spoon" [busybody], is a hot-headed one, and it is easy to turn him over from right to left and vice versa; what is good and fine to him today — it is not out of the question that tomorrow it will be loathsome and bad beyond endurance.
It goes without saying that under these conditions our fear is a well-founded one, and we would like our brethren to pay a little more attention to the importance of the question. Let everything be done with calm deliberation and with sensible calculation. Let people at long last be willing to understand that the representation of the Jewish kehilla must consist of the finest, most conscientious [?] and wisest people, who will understand how to take their place at the helm of Jewish life.
We need them now as never before, so that they do not allow Jewish honour to be sold and disgraced. On the contrary, like an armoured wall they must stand and guard Jewish purity and honesty, which is apt to raise our prestige, of which we are so greatly in need.
And therefore it must on no account whatever be allowed that everyone "make the Sabbath for himself". Let us not break up our forces, for in strength lie unity and power, might and awareness, of which we are enormously in need in the present era.

"Będzin's City Fathers
Upon my life, it has already become loathsome and repugnant [?] from all the talking and writing. How many times, for instance, have we drawn the attention of the Będzin councillors of the town council to their fallen state [?] and fragmentation? How much shame and disgrace and humiliation do they bring upon Jewish Będzin when they appear in the town council in the name of the Jewish public? If it pains us when our representatives do not stand at the proper level within our own four cubits, when our communal life is mocked there, then what satisfaction can we have when the same deeds are done in the town council, when it comes to the point that the Jewish public is insulted and spat upon, and none other than we ourselves bring it about that all this evil is poured out on Jewish heads. If one man wants to trip up another, to settle accounts with him so that he remembers it for generations, he finds the most suitable place for it in the town council, and our neighbours, naturally, derive satisfaction from it. Yes, they swell with delight at our "comradeship" "and parliamentarism". Meanwhile we are slapped at every step, and the Jewish councillors are exploited for the benefit of interests opposed to ours. Today the municipal budget is under consideration. One would think it a matter that ought to interest our councillors most of all, for we have, after all, a very great stake in it — and yet with what indifference do the Jewish councillors receive it? They are so little at home in the matter that, in order to obtain a subsidy of a few hundred złoty for some institution or other, they are ready to agree to burden the town with a new tax, which will cost all classes a fortune. Such clumsiness has surely never existed among the Jews in the town council; hardly had it come to the budget, they used to go there well-informed, prepared — and today, not only does one have no idea of all this, each man only looks to play a Turkish trick on the other — and let him remember me...
That is what people go into the town council for. And the question arises: is this permitted? May one act like this, either from the communal or from the human point of view? How are people who are, one would think, conscious human beings not ashamed to make themselves so ridiculous in the eyes of our neighbours, whereby they debase both our honour and their own, and this causes them to be held cheap as Jewish representatives.
How long, then, can such contempt continue, with which our representatives are, as it appears, quite content?
Will our city fathers really not look around and see how low they have fallen, and not seek a means of rescuing their prestige?
It is a question to which one ought to receive a matter-of-fact answer.

Our World Congress
The date of the World Jewish Congress is drawing near, and people are beginning to occupy themselves with this very important question. The interest, it appears, becomes the more important the nearer it comes.
In fact, people began long ago to talk about realising this Congress, only they could not come to terms among themselves. It is, after all, a rule: as many Jews, so many opinions; one pulled this way and the other, as usual, that way. The squabbles went on so long that there was nothing left to argue about, and for lack of any alternative people had to agree, first of all, to convene the first all-world Jewish Congress.
Among us people squabbled and split hairs, and meanwhile time did its work. Our situation in all countries became worse and graver, so that it was realised that we cannot permit ourselves to play at high politics, and people finally arrived at the conviction that convening the planned Congress is a matter of the greatest necessity. We must come together and express before the wide world our bitter sorrow and anger.
We want to tell the world that the Jewish people wants, like all the peoples of the world, to have the right to live and to work, and a place of rest after work.
Selekt.
